title.zh: 卷四百二十三 列傳第一百八十二 吳泳 徐範 李韶 王邁 史彌鞏 陳塤 趙與𥲅 李大同 黃㽦 楊大異
title.en: Volume 423 Biographies 182: Wu Yong; Xu Fan; Li Shao; Wang Mai; Shi Migong; Chen Xun; Zhao Yuchou; Li Datong; Huang Xun; Yang Dayi
title.raw: 卷四百二十三 列傳第一百八十二 吳泳 徐範 李韶 王邁 史彌鞏 陳塤 趙與𥲅 李大同 黃㽦 楊大異 Volume 423 Biographies 182: Wu Yong; Xu Fan; Li Shao; Wang Mai; Shi Migong; Chen Xun; Zhao Yuchou; Li Datong; Huang Xun; Yang Dayi

sentences.zh: 吳泳徐範李韶王邁史彌鞏陳塤

translations.literal: Wu Yong, Xu Fan, Li Shao, Wang Mai, Shi Migong, Chen Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yong, Xu Fan, Li Shao, Wang Mai, Shi Migong, and Chen Xun.

translations.literal: 〈(Zimeng)
translations.idiomatic: 〈The name is also written Zimeng.〉

sentences.zh: 趙與芮李大同黃┿楊大異

translations.literal: Zhao Yurui, Li Datong, Huang [damaged character], Yang Dayi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yurui, Li Datong, Huang Xun, and Yang Dayi.

sentences.zh: 吳泳，字叔永，潼川人。

translations.literal: Wu Yong, courtesy name Shuyong, was a native of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yong, whose courtesy name was Shuyong, came from Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年進士，歷官為軍器少監，行太府寺丞，行校書郎，升秘書丞兼權司封郎官，兼樞密院編修官，升著作郎，時暫兼權直舍人院。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination. He successively served as Vice Director of the Armory, Acting Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, Acting Collator, was promoted to Secretary of the Secretariat and concurrently Acting Registrar in the Bureau of Audience, and concurrently Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs; he was promoted to Gentleman Compiler and for a time concurrently served as Acting Director of the Drafting Office.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1209 and rose through a string of posts: Vice Director of the Armory, acting vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, acting collator, then Secretary of the Secretariat with concurrent acting duties in the Bureau of Audience and as a compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs. He was promoted to Gentleman Compiler and briefly served as acting director of the Drafting Office as well.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：“願陛下養心，以清明約己，以恭儉進德，以剛毅發強，毋以旨酒違善言，毋以嬖禦嫉莊士，毋以靡曼之色伐天性。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he said: "I wish Your Majesty would nourish the heart, with clarity and restraint in self-discipline, with reverence and frugality in advancing virtue, with firmness and vigor in strengthening resolve—do not let fine wine turn you from good counsel, do not let favored attendants make you jealous of upright men, do not let voluptuous beauty erode your innate nature.
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating audience he urged the emperor: "I ask that Your Majesty cultivate the inner self—govern yourself with clarity and restraint, advance in virtue through reverence and frugality, and strengthen your resolve with firmness and vigor. Do not let fine wine turn you from sound advice; do not let favored attendants breed jealousy of upright ministers; do not let voluptuous beauty wear away your natural disposition.

sentences.zh: 杜漸防微，澄源正本，使君身之所自立者先有其地。

translations.literal: Check the gradual and guard against the slight; clarify the source and rectify the root, so that where the ruler's person is to stand firm there is first a place for it.
translations.idiomatic: Check decline at its first signs, guard against the smallest faults, clarify the source and rectify the root, so that the ruler's own footing is secure before all else.

sentences.zh: 夫然後移所留之聰明以經世務，移所舍之精神以強國政，移所用之心力以恤疲民，移所當省之浮費以犒邊上久戍之士，則不惟可以消弭災變，攘除奸兇，殄滅寇賊，雖以是建久安長治之策可也。”

translations.literal: Only then shift the intelligence you have held back to ordering the affairs of the age, shift the spirit you have set aside to strengthening state administration, shift the mind and strength you have spent elsewhere to relieving the weary people, shift the wasteful expenditures that ought to be cut to rewarding the long-garrisoned troops on the frontier—then not only can you dispel calamities and omens, drive off treacherous villains, and exterminate bandits and rebels; even a policy of lasting peace and long stability may be built on this."
translations.idiomatic: Only then turn the intelligence you have withheld to governing the realm, the energy you have spared to strengthening the state, the effort you have spent elsewhere to relieving a weary populace, and the wasteful expenditures that should be cut to rewarding troops who have long stood guard on the frontier. Then you will not only dispel omens and calamities, drive off traitors, and crush rebels—you may even lay the foundations of enduring peace and stable rule."

sentences.zh: 他日入對，又言：“誦往哲之遺言，進謀國之上策，實不過曰內修政事而已。

translations.literal: On another day, entering audience, he again said: "To recite the legacy words of past sages and advance the supreme stratagem for planning the state is in truth nothing more than saying: cultivate internal government.
translations.idiomatic: On another audience day he said again: "To recite the teachings of past sages and advance the highest strategy for the state comes down to one thing: strengthen government at home.

sentences.zh: 然所謂內修者，非但車馬器械之謂也。

translations.literal: Yet what is called internal cultivation is not merely a matter of chariots, horses, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: But internal cultivation means more than chariots, horses, and arms alone.

sentences.zh: 袞職之闕，所當修也；

translations.literal: The gaps in the ruler's own duties are what ought to be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's own failures of duty must be repaired;

sentences.zh: 官師之曠，所當修也；

translations.literal: the vacancies among officials and teachers are what ought to be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: vacancies among officials and instructors must be filled;

sentences.zh: 出令之所弗清，所當修也；

translations.literal: where issued orders are not clear is what ought to be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: where edicts are unclear must be clarified;

sentences.zh: 本兵之地弗嚴，所當修也；

translations.literal: where the root of military affairs is not strict is what ought to be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: where the foundations of military affairs are lax must be tightened;

sentences.zh: 直言敢諫之未得其職，所當修也；

translations.literal: where outspoken remonstrators have not obtained their proper posts is what ought to be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: where forthright remonstrators lack their proper posts must be set right;

sentences.zh: 折沖禦侮之弗堪其任，所當修也。

translations.literal: where those who repel enemies and guard against insult are unequal to their charge is what ought to be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: where those charged with repelling enemies are unequal to their task must be remedied.

sentences.zh: 陛下退修於其上，百官有司交修於其下，朝廷既正，人心既附，然後申警國人，精討軍實，合內修外攘為一事，神州赤縣，皆在吾指顧中矣。”

translations.literal: Your Majesty should withdraw to cultivate above; the hundred officials and functionaries should mutually cultivate below. Once the court is rectified and hearts are attached, then warn and alert the people of the realm, scrutinize military strength in detail, unite internal cultivation and external defense as one matter—the sacred land and red counties will all lie within our beck and call."
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty cultivate yourself above while officials cultivate their duties below. When the court is upright and the people's hearts are won, then rouse the nation, scrutinize military strength in earnest, and treat internal reform and external defense as one undertaking—the whole empire will lie within our grasp."

sentences.zh: 火災，應詔上封曰：“京城之災，京城之所見也。

translations.literal: When fire broke out, in response to an edict he submitted a sealed memorial saying: "The disaster in the capital is what the capital can see.
translations.idiomatic: After a fire, he submitted a sealed memorial in response to an imperial edict: "The disaster in the capital is visible in the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 四方有敗，陛下亦得而見之乎？

translations.literal: When there is ruin in the four quarters, can Your Majesty also see it?
translations.idiomatic: When the four quarters are in ruin, can Your Majesty see that as well?

sentences.zh: 夫慘莫慘於兵也，而連年不戢，則甚於火矣。

translations.literal: Of miseries none is more miserable than war, yet when war goes unchecked year after year, it is worse than fire.
translations.idiomatic: No misery exceeds that of war, yet when war rages unchecked year after year, it is worse than any fire.

sentences.zh: 酷莫酷於吏也，而頻歲橫征，則猛於火矣。

translations.literal: Of cruelties none is more cruel than officials, yet when ruthless levies come year after year, they are fiercer than fire.
translations.idiomatic: No cruelty exceeds that of corrupt officials, yet when ruthless levies come year after year, they are more savage than fire.

sentences.zh: 閩之民困於盜，浙之民困於水，蜀之民困於兵。

translations.literal: The people of Min are afflicted by bandits, the people of Zhe by flood, the people of Shu by war.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian suffer from banditry, those of Zhejiang from flood, and those of Sichuan from war.

sentences.zh: 橫斂之原既不澄於上，包苴之根又不絕於下。

translations.literal: The source of ruthless exactions is not cleared above, and the root of bribery parcels is not cut off below.
translations.idiomatic: The source of ruthless exactions is not cleared above, and the root of bribery is not severed below.

sentences.zh: 譬彼壞木，疾用無枝，而內涸之形見矣。”

translations.literal: It is like a ruined tree, swiftly used up until it has no branches, and the form of inward desiccation already appears."
translations.idiomatic: It is like a ruined tree stripped of branches in haste—the inward withering is already plain to see."

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監，兼權中書舍人，尋遷起居舍人兼權吏部侍郎，兼直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Acting Drafting Secretary; soon he was transferred to Attendant Diarist and concurrently Acting Vice Minister of Personnel, and concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent acting duties as drafting secretary, then to Attendant Diarist with concurrent acting vice minister of personnel and membership in the Hanlin Institute.

sentences.zh: 疏言：“世之識治體而憂時幾者，以為天運將變矣，世道將降矣，國論將更矣，正人將引去而舊人將登用矣。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Those in the world who understand the body of governance and worry over the turning of the times believe that the mandate of Heaven is about to change, the way of the age is about to decline, state policy is about to shift, upright men are about to withdraw while old hands are about to be employed.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Those who understand governance and watch the times fear that Heaven's mandate is shifting, the moral order declining, national policy changing, upright men about to leave office while old factions return to power.

sentences.zh: 執持初意，封植正論，茲非砥柱傾頹之時乎？

translations.literal: To hold fast to the original intent and nurture upright discourse—is this not the hour when the pillar in midstream is toppling?
translations.idiomatic: To hold fast to your original purpose and uphold honest debate—is this not the hour when the pillar in midstream is giving way?

sentences.zh: 若使廉通敏慧者專治財賦，淑慎曉暢者專禦軍旅，明清敬謹者專典刑獄，經術通明使道訓典，文雅麗則使作訓辭，秉節堅厲使備風憲，奉法循理使居牧守，剛直有守者不聽其引去，恬退無競者不聽其裏居，功名慷慨者不佚之以祠庭，言論闿爽者不置之於外服，隨才器使，各盡其分，則短長小大，安有不適用者哉！”

translations.literal: If the incorrupt, penetrating, and keen were put solely in charge of revenue, the virtuous, cautious, and well-informed solely in command of armies, the clear, bright, reverent, and careful solely in charge of penal law, those versed in the classics and penetrating in doctrine made to oversee ritual and canon, the refined and elegant made to compose edifying prose, those who hold integrity firm and stern made to serve in censorial posts, those who follow law and reason made to hold prefectural governorships—if men of upright integrity and firm principle were not allowed to withdraw, the tranquil and retiring and uncontentious were not allowed to live in seclusion, men of generous achievement were not idled away in temple stipends, and men of open and forthright discourse were not placed in outer appointments—if each were employed according to talent and capacity and each fulfilled his part, then whether short or long, small or great, how could any fail to find fitting use!"
translations.idiomatic: Let the incorrupt and capable manage finance alone; the prudent and knowledgeable command armies; the clear-minded and careful oversee justice; scholars of the classics supervise ritual and law; the refined draft edifying prose; the stern serve as censors; the law-abiding govern the provinces. Do not let upright men resign, the modest retire to seclusion, men of achievement languish on temple stipends, or outspoken critics be banished to distant posts. Match talent to duty and each will find his place—what office, great or small, would then go unfilled?"

sentences.zh: 又言謹政體、正道揆、厲臣節、綜軍務四事。

translations.literal: He also spoke of four matters: careful governance of the polity, rectifying the chief ministers, strengthening official integrity, and coordinating military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged four reforms: careful governance, upright chief ministers, stronger official integrity, and coordinated military affairs.

sentences.zh: 權刑部尚書兼修玉牒，以寶章閣直學士知寧國府，提舉太平興國宮，進寶章閣學士，差知溫州。

translations.literal: He was Acting Minister of Justice and concurrently Compiler of the Imperial Genealogy; as Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion he governed Ningguo Prefecture and oversaw the Taiping Xingguo Palace; he was advanced to Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion and assigned to govern Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Minister of Justice while compiling the imperial genealogy, then as Baozhang Pavilion academician and prefect of Ningguo, with charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace. Promoted to full academician of the pavilion, he was assigned to Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 赴官，道間聞溫州饑，至處州，乞蠲租科降，救餓者四萬八千有奇，放夏稅一十二萬有奇，秋苗二萬八千有奇，病者復與之藥。

translations.literal: On his way to take office he heard on the road that Wenzhou was in famine. Reaching Chuzhou, he begged remission and reduction of tax levies, relieved more than forty-eight thousand starving people, remitted more than one hundred twenty thousand in summer tax, more than twenty-eight thousand in autumn grain tax, and also gave medicine to the sick.
translations.idiomatic: En route to his post he learned that Wenzhou was famine-stricken. At Chuzhou he secured tax remissions and reductions, fed more than forty-eight thousand starving people, remitted over 120,000 units of summer tax and 28,000 of autumn grain tax, and provided medicine to the sick.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜衣帶鞍馬。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted robes, belt, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of this, it rewarded him with robes, a belt, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 改知泉州，以言罷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Quanzhou and was dismissed because of his remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Quanzhou but was dismissed after his outspoken memorials.

sentences.zh: 所著有《鶴林集》。

translations.literal: His writings include the Collected Works from the Crane Grove.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings survive as the Crane Grove Anthology.

sentences.zh: 徐範，字彜父，福州候官人。

translations.literal: Xu Fan, courtesy name Yifu, was a native of Houguan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fan, whose courtesy name was Yifu, came from Houguan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，刻苦授徒以養母。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he taught pupils with bitter diligence to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he supported his mother by teaching pupils with tireless diligence.

sentences.zh: 與兄同舉於鄉，入太學，未嘗以疾言遽色先人。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother passed the provincial examination together, entered the Imperial College, and never once spoke harshly or showed a sudden angry countenance before those senior to him.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother passed the provincial examination together and entered the Imperial College, where he never spoke harshly or showed anger toward his seniors.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙汝愚去位，祭酒李祥、博士楊簡論救之，俱被斥逐。

translations.literal: When Chief Councillor Zhao Ruyu left office, Rector Li Xiang and Erudite Yang Jian argued in his defense; all were expelled and banished.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councillor Zhao Ruyu was removed, Rector Li Xiang and Erudite Yang Jian spoke in his defense; all were expelled and banished.

sentences.zh: 同舍生議叩閽上書，書已具，有閩士亦署名，忽夜傳韓侂胄將置言者重辟，閩士怖，請削名，範之友亦勸止之。

translations.literal: Fellow students in the dormitory proposed knocking at the palace gate to submit a memorial; the document was already prepared and a Fujian student had also signed. Suddenly that night word spread that Han Tuozhou would impose heavy punishment on the petitioners. The Fujian student was terrified and asked to have his name struck off; Xu's friends also urged him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow students proposed a petition at the palace gate. The memorial was ready and a Fujian student had signed it, but that night word spread that Han Tuozhou would punish the petitioners severely. The Fujian student panicked and asked to withdraw his name, and Xu's friends urged him to do the same.

sentences.zh: 範慨然曰：“業已書名矣，尚何變？”

translations.literal: Xu said with emotion: "The name is already written—what is there to change?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu said firmly: "My name is already on it—why should I change?"

sentences.zh: 書奏，侂胄果大怒，謂其扇搖國是，各送五百里編管。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Tuozhou was indeed greatly enraged, saying they had stirred and shaken the national consensus, and each was sent five hundred li into supervised exile.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the court, Tuozhou was furious, accusing them of subverting state policy, and had each exiled five hundred li under guard.

sentences.zh: 範謫臨海，與兄歸同往，禁錮十餘年。

translations.literal: Fan was banished to Linhai; he and his elder brother Gui went together and were confined for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was banished to Linhai. He and his elder brother Gui went into exile together and remained confined for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 登嘉定元年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1208.

sentences.zh: 授清江縣尉，辟江、淮制置司準備差遣。

translations.literal: He was appointed county lieutenant of Qingjiang and was recruited as preparatory agent of the Jiang-Huai Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed lieutenant of Qingjiang County and recruited as a preparatory agent of the Jiang-Huai Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 屬邊事紛糾，營砦子弟募隸軍籍者未及涅，洶洶相驚。

translations.literal: At a time when frontier affairs were in turmoil, camp youths recruited into military registers who had not yet been tattooed were in a ferment of mutual alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier affairs were in turmoil. Young men recruited from the camps into military service who had not yet been tattooed grew restless and alarmed one another.

sentences.zh: 一夕，秉燭招刺千餘人，踴躍爭奮。

translations.literal: In one night, by candlelight he summoned and tattooed more than a thousand men, who leapt up competing to show zeal.
translations.idiomatic: In a single night, working by candlelight, he summoned and tattooed more than a thousand men, who leapt forward eager to serve.

sentences.zh: 差主管戶部架閣，改太學錄，遷國子監主簿。

translations.literal: He was assigned to supervise the archives of the Ministry of Revenue, was transferred to Recorder of the Imperial College, and was promoted to Registrar of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Ministry of Revenue archives, then made recorder of the Imperial College and promoted to registrar of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：“時平，不急之務、無用之官，猶當痛加裁節，矧多事之秋，所貴全萬民之命，紓一時之急，獨奈何坐視其無救而以虛文自蔽哉！

translations.literal: Entering audience, he said: "In times of peace, tasks that are not urgent and offices that are useless should still be sharply cut back—how much more in a season of many troubles, when what is prized is preserving the lives of the myriad people and easing the urgency of the moment. How can we alone sit by watching them beyond rescue and screen ourselves with empty documents!
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said: "Even in peaceful times, nonessential tasks and useless offices should be sharply cut. In troubled times, when the people's lives hang in the balance, how can we sit idle and hide behind empty paperwork?

sentences.zh: 願懲既往之失，廢無用之文，一意養民，以培國本。”

translations.literal: I wish to punish past errors, abolish useless documents, with single intent nourish the people, and thereby strengthen the foundation of the state."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that past errors be corrected, useless paperwork abolished, and every effort bent to nourishing the people and strengthening the nation's foundation."

sentences.zh: 丐外，添差通判澤州。

translations.literal: He begged an outer appointment and was given an additional assignment as vice prefect of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a provincial post and was given an additional assignment as vice prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 湖湘大旱，振救多所裨益。

translations.literal: When Hunan and Hubei suffered great drought, his relief efforts were of much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought in Hunan and Hubei, his relief work proved highly effective.

sentences.zh: 知邵武軍，尋召赴行在，言：“功利不若道德，刑罰不若恩厚，雜伯不若純王，異端不若儒術，諛佞不若直諫，便嬖不若正人，奢侈不若詩書，盤遊不若節儉，玩好不若宵衣旰食，窮黷不若偃兵息民。

translations.literal: He governed Shaowu Commandery; soon he was summoned to the temporary capital and said: "Utility and profit are not as good as virtue and the Way; punishments are not as good as kindness and generosity; mixed hegemony is not as good as pure kingship; heterodox teachings are not as good as Confucian learning; flattery and sycophancy are not as good as straightforward remonstrance; favored minions are not as good as upright men; extravagance is not as good as the Odes and Documents; roaming pleasure is not as good as frugality; indulgence in favorites is not as good as working late into the night and rising early; exhausting warfare is not as good as laying down arms and giving the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Shaowu Commandery and was soon summoned to the temporary capital, where he said: "Profit is inferior to virtue, punishment to kindness, hegemony to true kingship, heterodoxy to Confucian learning, flattery to honest remonstrance, favorites to upright men, extravagance to the classics, pleasure-seeking to frugality, indulgence to tireless labor for the state, and endless war to laying down arms and giving the people rest.

sentences.zh: 是非兩立，明白易見。

translations.literal: Right and wrong stand opposed; the distinction is clear and easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong stand in plain opposition, clear for all to see.

sentences.zh: 幾微之際，大體所關。

translations.literal: At the subtle turning point, the great pattern is at stake.
translations.idiomatic: At subtle turning points, the fate of the whole polity hangs in the balance.

sentences.zh: 積習不移，治道舛矣。”

translations.literal: If accumulated habits are not changed, the way of governance is already astray."
translations.idiomatic: If entrenched habits are not changed, the path of governance is already lost."

sentences.zh: 遷國子監丞，徙太常丞，權都官郎官，改秘書丞、著作郎、起居郎、兼國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, moved to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, acted as Registrar in the Bureau of Justice, and was changed to Secretary of the Secretariat, Gentleman Compiler, Gentleman Attendant, and concurrently Compiler of the National History and Reviser of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education, then vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, acting registrar in the Bureau of Justice, and finally secretary of the Secretariat, gentleman compiler, gentleman attendant, with concurrent duties compiling the National History and revising the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 以朝奉大夫致仕。

translations.literal: He retired with the rank of Grandee for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Grandee for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈朝請大夫、集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grandee for Imperial Audience and Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as Grandee for Imperial Audience and compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence.

sentences.zh: 李韶，字元善，彌遜之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Li Shao, courtesy name Yuanshan, was the great-grandson of Li Miyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao, whose courtesy name was Yuanshan, was the great-grandson of Li Miyi.

sentences.zh: 父文饒，為臺州司理參軍，每謂人曰：“吾司臬多陰德，後有興者。”

translations.literal: His father Wenrao served as judicial assistant of Taizhou and often told people: "In my office of justice I have accumulated much hidden virtue; later there will be one who rises."
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenrao served as judicial assistant in Taizhou and often said: "In my post I have done much good in secret; our line will prosper."

sentences.zh: 韶五歲，能賦梅花。

translations.literal: At five, Shao could compose a fu on plum blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: At five, Shao could already compose a poem on plum blossoms.

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年，與其兄寧同舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiading he and his elder brother Ning passed the jinshi examination together.
translations.idiomatic: In 1211 he and his elder brother Ning passed the jinshi examination together.

sentences.zh: 調南雄州教授。

translations.literal: He was assigned as professor of Nanxiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at Nanxiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 校文廣州，時有當國之親故私報所業，韶卻之。

translations.literal: While examining essays in Guangzhou, a kinsman of those in power privately reported his own work to him; Shao refused it.
translations.idiomatic: While grading examinations in Guangzhou, a relative of the ruling faction privately sent him his own work; Shao refused it.

sentences.zh: 調慶元。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 丞相史彌遠薦士充學職，韶不與。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan recommended scholars to fill academic posts; Shao would not go along.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan recommended candidates for academic posts, Shao would not cooperate.

sentences.zh: 袁燮求學宮射圃益其居，亦不與，燮以此更敬韶。

translations.literal: Yuan Xie asked to enlarge his residence with the academy archery ground; Shao again would not agree, and Xie for this reason respected Shao all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xie sought to expand his residence into the academy archery ground, Shao again refused, and Yuan respected him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 以廉勤薦，遷主管三省架閣文字，遷太學正，改太學博士。

translations.literal: Recommended for integrity and diligence, he was transferred to supervise archival documents of the Three Departments, was transferred to Director of the Imperial College, and was changed to Erudite of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for integrity and diligence, he rose to supervise the archives of the Three Departments, then became director and erudite of the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 上封事諫濟王竑獄，且以書曉彌遠，言甚懇到。

translations.literal: He submitted a sealed memorial remonstrating against the case of Prince Ji, and also wrote to enlighten Miyuan; his words were very earnest and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a sealed memorial protesting the case of Prince Ji and wrote earnestly to Miyuan to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 又救太學生寧式，迕學官。

translations.literal: He also rescued the Imperial College student Ning Shi, running counter to the college officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also defended the Imperial College student Ning Shi, defying the college authorities.

sentences.zh: 丐外，添差通判泉州。

translations.literal: He begged an outer appointment and was given an additional assignment as vice prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a provincial post and was given an additional assignment as vice prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡守遊九功素清嚴，獨異顧韶。

translations.literal: The prefect You Jiugong was by nature stern and austere, yet he alone treated Shao with special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect You Jiugong was known for his stern integrity, yet he singled Shao out for special regard.

sentences.zh: 改知道州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 葺周惇頤故居，錄其子孫於學宮，且周其家。

translations.literal: He repaired the former residence of Zhou Dunyi, enrolled his descendants in the academy, and also provided for his household.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Zhou Dunyi's former home, enrolled his descendants in the local academy, and provided for the family.

sentences.zh: 紹定四年，行都災，韶應詔言事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoding the temporary capital suffered disaster; Shao responded to an edict and spoke on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1231, when disaster struck the temporary capital, Shao submitted memorials in response to an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 提舉福建市舶。

translations.literal: He was made overseer of the Fujian maritime trade bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed overseer of Fujian's maritime trade bureau.

sentences.zh: 會星變，又應詔言事。

translations.literal: When a stellar anomaly occurred, he again responded to an edict and spoke on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When a stellar anomaly appeared, he again submitted memorials in response to an edict.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監丞，改知泉州兼市舶。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and was changed to govern Quanzhou while concurrently overseeing maritime trade.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the Directorate of Education, then appointed prefect of Quanzhou with concurrent charge of maritime trade.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，召。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1234 he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉太府寺丞，遷都官郎官，遷尚左郎官。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was promoted to Registrar in the Bureau of Justice, and was promoted to Registrar in the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then registrar in the Bureau of Justice and the Left Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜右正言。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 奏乞以國事、邊防二事專委丞相鄭清之、喬行簡各任責。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging that the two matters of state affairs and frontier defense be entrusted solely to Chief Councillors Zheng Qingzhi and Qiao Xingjian, each to bear responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that state affairs and frontier defense be entrusted solely to Chief Councillors Zheng Qingzhi and Qiao Xingjian, each bearing full responsibility.

sentences.zh: 論汰兵、節財及襄、蜀邊防。

translations.literal: He discussed reducing troops, economizing finances, and the frontier defenses of Xiang and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He urged troop reductions, fiscal restraint, and stronger defenses on the Xiangyang and Sichuan frontiers.

sentences.zh: 又論史嵩之、王遂和戰異議，迄無成功，請出遂於要藩，易嵩之於邊面，使各盡其才。

translations.literal: He also discussed Shi Songzhi and Wang Sui, whose views on war and peace differed and who to the end achieved no success, and asked that Sui be sent out to an important prefecture and Songzhi be moved to a frontier post so that each might fully employ his talent.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Shi Songzhi and Wang Sui, divided over war and peace, had achieved nothing, and asked that Wang be sent to an important prefecture and Shi to a frontier command so each could use his talents fully.

sentences.zh: 史宅之將守袁州，韶率同列一再劾之。

translations.literal: When Shi Zhaizhi was about to govern Yuanzhou, Shao led his colleagues in impeaching him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zhaizhi was appointed to govern Yuanzhou, Shao led his colleagues in repeated impeachments.

sentences.zh: 俱不報。

translations.literal: None received response.
translations.idiomatic: None received a response.

sentences.zh: 乞解言職，拜殿中侍御史，辭，不允。

translations.literal: He begged to be released from his remonstrating post and was appointed Palace Attendant Censor; he declined, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave his remonstrating post and was appointed Palace Attendant Censor. He declined, but the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：“頃同臣居言職者四人，未逾月徐清叟去，未三月杜範、吳昌裔免，獨臣尚就列。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: "Recently four of us held remonstrating posts together. Within a month Xu Qingsou left; within three months Du Fan and Wu Changyi were dismissed; I alone remain in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Recently four of us held remonstrating posts. Within a month Xu Qingsou left; within three months Du Fan and Wu Changyi were dismissed. I alone remain.

sentences.zh: 清叟昨言‘三漸’，臣繼其說，李宗勉又繼之，陛下初不加怒，而清叟竟去，猶曰清叟倡之也。

translations.literal: Yesterday Qingsou spoke of the 'three gradual declines'; I followed his argument, and Li Zongmian followed again. Your Majesty at first showed no anger, yet Qingsou in the end left, and it was still said that Qingsou had initiated it.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsou spoke of the 'three gradual declines'; I followed his argument, and Li Zongmian followed mine. Your Majesty showed no anger at first, yet Qingsou was dismissed—and still they said he had led the way.

sentences.zh: 今臣與範、昌裔言，未嘗不相表裏，二臣出臺，臣獨留，豈臣言不加切於二臣邪？

translations.literal: Now what Fan, Changyi, and I said was never not mutually inside and outside. The two ministers left the Censorate and I alone remain—can it be that my words were not more cutting than those of the two ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Fan, Changyi, and I spoke as one. They were dismissed and I remain—can my words have been less forceful than theirs?

sentences.zh: 抑先去二臣以警臣，使知擇而後言邪？

translations.literal: Or was it rather that the two ministers were removed first to warn me, so that I would know to choose before speaking?
translations.idiomatic: Or were they dismissed first to warn me—to teach me to choose my words more carefully?

sentences.zh: 清叟所言‘三漸’，臣猶以為未甚切。

translations.literal: As for the 'three gradual declines' that Qingsou spoke of, I still think they were not very cutting.
translations.idiomatic: As for Qingsou's 'three gradual declines,' I still think they did not go far enough.

sentences.zh: 今國柄有陵夷之漸，士氣有委靡之漸，主勢有孤立之漸，宗社有阽危之漸，上下偷安，以人言為諱，此意不改，其禍豈直三漸而已。”

translations.literal: Now state power has a gradual decline of erosion, scholar-official morale a gradual decline of lassitude, the ruler's position a gradual decline into isolation, and the altars of soil and grain a gradual decline into peril on the brink. Above and below seek ease in complacency and treat human speech as taboo. If this intent is not changed, will the calamity be only three gradual declines?
translations.idiomatic: Today state power erodes by degrees, official morale wilts, the throne grows isolated, and the dynasty stands on the brink. Court and country seek comfort in complacency and treat honest speech as forbidden. If this does not change, the disaster will be far worse than three gradual declines alone."

sentences.zh: 時魏了翁罷督予祠，韶訟曰：“了翁刻誌問學，幾四十年，忠言讜論，載在國史，去就出處，具有本末。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Liaoweng had been dismissed from supervision and granted a temple stipend. Shao pleaded on his behalf saying: "Liaoweng has carved his will into learning for nearly forty years; loyal words and forthright discourse are recorded in the national history; his departures and arrivals, exits and entries, all have beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Liaoweng was dismissed from his supervisory post and granted a temple stipend, Shao pleaded for him: "Liaoweng has devoted nearly forty years to learning. His loyal counsel fills the national histories, and his career has a clear record from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 端平收召，論事益切。

translations.literal: In Duanping he was recalled; his discussion of affairs grew still more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in the Duanping era, he spoke on state affairs with growing urgency.

sentences.zh: 去年督府之遣，體統不一，識者逆知其無功。

translations.literal: Last year, when the supervisory headquarters sent him out, the institutional order was not unified; those with insight foresaw in advance that it would be without success.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's dispatch to the supervisory headquarters lacked unified command, and perceptive observers knew in advance it would fail.

sentences.zh: 了翁迫於君命，黽勉驅馳，未有大闕，襄州變出肘腋，未可以為了翁罪。

translations.literal: Liaoweng was compelled by the ruler's command and strove with effort in hurried service; he had no great fault. The upheaval at Xiangzhou arose from within his own arm—this cannot be made Liaoweng's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoweng obeyed the emperor's command and served diligently without major fault. The upheaval at Xiangzhou arose from within his own camp—it cannot be laid at his door.

sentences.zh: 樞庭之召，未幾改鎮，改鎮未久，有旨予祠。

translations.literal: When the Bureau of Military Affairs summoned him, before long he was transferred to a commandery post; not long after the transfer, an edict granted him a temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Bureau of Military Affairs, he was soon transferred to a regional command, and not long after that granted a temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 不知國家四十年來收拾人才，燁然有稱如了翁者幾人？

translations.literal: Does the state not know that in forty years of gathering talent, how many men of shining reputation like Liaoweng are there?
translations.idiomatic: In forty years of gathering talent for the state, how many men of Liaoweng's stature and reputation can be named?

sentences.zh: 願亟召還，處以臺輔。”

translations.literal: I wish he might quickly be recalled and placed in a censorial or chief-ministerial post."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that he be recalled at once and placed among the chief ministers and censors."

sentences.zh: 又劾奏陳洵益刑余腐夫，粗通文墨，掃除賤隸，竊弄威權，乞予洵益外祠。

translations.literal: He also impeached Chen Xunyi, a man left over from punishment, a rotten fellow who barely knew letters, a sweeper and base menial who usurped authority, and begged that Xunyi be given an outer temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Chen Xunyi, a convicted remnant and corrupt mediocrity who barely knew letters, a menial who had seized power, and asked that he be given an outer temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 劾女冠吳知古在宮掖招權納賄，宜出之禁庭。

translations.literal: He impeached the female Taoist Wu Zhigu for wielding power and taking bribes within the palace women's quarters; she should be removed from the forbidden court.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the Taoist priestess Wu Zhigu for wielding power and taking bribes within the inner palace, and urged that she be expelled from the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，韶還笏殿陛乞歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Shao returned his tablet on the palace steps and begged to go home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged. Shao returned his court tablet on the palace steps and begged to resign.

sentences.zh: 會祀明堂，雷電，免二相，韶權工部侍郎、正言，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was being sacrificed to, thunder and lightning struck; the two chief councillors were dismissed. Shao was made Acting Vice Minister of Works and Remonstrator, and was transferred to Attendant Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: During sacrifices at the Bright Hall, thunder and lightning struck and both chief councillors were dismissed. Shao was made acting vice minister of works and remonstrator, then promoted to attendant diarist.

sentences.zh: 復疏洵益、知古，不報。

translations.literal: He again memorialized against Xunyi and Zhigu; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized against Xunyi and Zhigu, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 辭新命，不許。

translations.literal: He declined the new appointment; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the new appointment, but was not allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 應詔上封事，幾數千言。

translations.literal: In response to an edict he submitted a sealed memorial of nearly several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: In response to an edict he submitted a sealed memorial of several thousand words.

sentences.zh: 帝諭左右曰：“李韶真有愛朕憂國之心。”

translations.literal: The emperor instructed those beside him saying: "Li Shao truly has a heart that loves me and worries for the state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants: "Li Shao truly loves me and cares for the state."

sentences.zh: 凡三辭不獲，以生死祈哀乞去。

translations.literal: He declined three times without success and begged to leave, pleading with life and death in supplication.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times without success and begged to leave, pleading with his life at stake.

sentences.zh: 帝蹙額謂韶曰：“曲為朕留。”

translations.literal: The emperor knit his brow and said to Shao: "Bend your will and stay for my sake."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor frowned and said to Shao: "Do me this favor and stay."

sentences.zh: 退，復累疏乞補外，以集英殿修撰知漳州，號稱廉平。

translations.literal: After withdrawing, he again submitted repeated memorials begging for an outer appointment and was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Zhangzhou, where he was known as incorrupt and fair.
translations.idiomatic: After he withdrew, he submitted repeated memorials asking for a provincial post and was appointed compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Zhangzhou, where he earned a reputation for integrity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 朝廷分遣部使者諸路稱提官楮，韶疏極言其敝。

translations.literal: The court dispatched departmental envoys to the circuits to promote paper currency; Shao memorialized forcefully on its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: When the court dispatched envoys to the circuits to promote paper currency, Shao memorialized forcefully against the policy's abuses.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年，召。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaxi he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1238 he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 明年，上疏乞寢召命云：

translations.literal: The next year he submitted a memorial begging that the summons be withdrawn, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized asking that the summons be withdrawn, writing:

sentences.zh: 端平以來，天下之患，莫大於敵兵歲至，和不可，戰不能，楮券日輕，民生流離，物價踴貴，遂至事無可為。

translations.literal: Since Duanping, of the world's afflictions none is greater than enemy troops arriving year after year: peace cannot be made, war cannot be fought, paper notes grow lighter daily, the people's lives drift in exile, prices leap upward, until affairs reach the point where nothing can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Duanping era, no affliction has exceeded the enemy's annual incursions: peace is impossible, war unavailing, paper currency daily depreciates, the people are displaced, prices soar, and the state has reached the point where nothing can be done.

sentences.zh: 臣竊論以為必自上始，九重菲衣惡食，臥薪嘗膽，使上下改慮易聽，然後可圖。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to argue that it must begin from above: in the ninefold precincts, coarse clothes and poor food, sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall, so that above and below change their thoughts and readily listen—only then can plans be made.
translations.idiomatic: I believe reform must begin at the top: the emperor must live plainly, endure hardship as King Goujian did, and change the court's thinking—only then can we plan recovery.

sentences.zh: 今二患益深，雖欲效忠，他莫有以為說。

translations.literal: Now the two afflictions grow still deeper; though I wish to serve loyally, I have nothing else with which to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Now both afflictions have deepened. Though I wish to serve loyally, I have nothing further to say.

sentences.zh: 此其不敢進者一。

translations.literal: This is the first reason I dare not advance.
translations.idiomatic: This is my first reason for not coming forward.

sentences.zh: 史宅之，故相子，予郡，外議皆謂扳援之徒將自是復用，故嘗論列至再。

translations.literal: Shi Zhaizhi, son of a former chief councillor, was given a prefecture; outside opinion all said that those who pull connections would from this be employed again, so I once discussed and listed this twice.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhaizhi, son of a former chief councillor, was given a prefecture. Public opinion held that factional hangers-on would return to power, and I had twice spoken against this.

sentences.zh: 今聖斷赫然，用舍由己，人才一變矣。

translations.literal: Now the sacred decision is brilliant and clear; employment and dismissal are in Your Majesty's own hands, and talent has wholly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's decision is clear: appointments and dismissals are in your hands, and the roster of talent has changed entirely.

sentences.zh: 環視前日在廷之臣，流落擯棄，臣雖欲貪進，未知所以處其身。

translations.literal: Looking around at the ministers who were at court the other day, cast out and discarded, though I wish to advance greedily, I do not know how to place myself.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at the ministers who were recently at court, now cast out and discarded, I do not know how I could advance even if I wished to.

sentences.zh: 此其不敢進者二。

translations.literal: This is the second reason I dare not advance.
translations.idiomatic: This is my second reason for not coming forward.

sentences.zh: 始臣為郎，蜀受兵方亟，廟堂已遣小使至，特起嵩之於家，而言者攻擊不已。

translations.literal: When I first served as a court gentleman, Shu was under urgent attack; the court had already sent a minor envoy, and Songzhi was specially raised from his home, yet remonstrators attacked without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When I first served at court, Sichuan was under heavy attack. The court had already sent envoys and specially recalled Songzhi from retirement, yet critics attacked him without cease.

sentences.zh: 臣妄論以為講和固非策，而首兵亦豈能無罪。

translations.literal: Your servant rashly argued that making peace was indeed no strategy, yet those who first urged war—how could they be without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: I argued then that peace was no solution, but those who had first urged war were hardly blameless either.

sentences.zh: 故居言路，首乞出高論者付以兵事，使稍知敵情者嘗試其說於閫外。

translations.literal: Therefore, while holding the remonstrating post, I first begged that those who held lofty arguments be sent out and entrusted with military affairs, so that those who somewhat knew enemy conditions might try their theories beyond the commander's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, while in my remonstrating post, I first asked that those who preached war be sent to command troops, so men who knew the enemy might test their theories in the field.

sentences.zh: 不知事勢推移，遂竟罷廢，而款敵無功者，白麻揚廷矣。

translations.literal: Who knew that as the situation shifted, they would in the end be dismissed, while those who treated with the enemy without success had white hemp edicts proclaimed in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Who knew that circumstances would shift so that the war party would be dismissed while those who had failed in negotiations against the enemy would be honored with imperial appointments proclaimed in court.

sentences.zh: 或者將議臣前日有所附會。

translations.literal: Some will perhaps discuss whether your servant the other day had some factional alignment.
translations.idiomatic: Some may say I was playing factions back then.

sentences.zh: 此臣重不敢進者三。

translations.literal: This is the third reason your servant again dares not advance.
translations.idiomatic: This is my third reason for not coming forward.

sentences.zh: 又臣昨彈內侍女冠，不行，退惟聖主高明，必不容其幹政。

translations.literal: Again, your servant yesterday impeached the palace eunuch and female Taoist; it was not carried out. On withdrawing I thought only that the sage ruler is enlightened and would surely not permit them to meddle in government.
translations.idiomatic: Again, I impeached the palace eunuch and Taoist priestess, but nothing was done. I withdrew trusting that a wise ruler would never permit them to meddle in government.

sentences.zh: 然未幾首相去位，臣亦出臺，傳聞其人謂臣受廟堂風旨，故決意丐外。

translations.literal: Yet before long the chief councillor left office and your servant also left the Censorate. It was rumored that those persons said your servant had received the court's secret instruction and therefore resolved to beg an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: Yet soon the chief councillor fell and I left the Censorate. Rumor held that those persons said I had acted on secret court instructions and therefore sought a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 今臣言迄不行，茍貪君命，竊恐或者譏臣向何所聞而去，今何所見而來。

translations.literal: Now your servant's words to the end are not carried out; if I greedily cling to the ruler's command, I secretly fear that some will ridicule me: on what did you hear when you left, and on what do you see when you come?
translations.idiomatic: Now my words still go unheeded. If I cling greedily to office, I fear some will mock me: what did you hear when you left, and what do you see now that you return?

sentences.zh: 此臣重不敢進者四。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason your servant again dares not advance.
translations.idiomatic: This is my fourth reason for not coming forward.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔趣赴闕，辭，遷戶部侍郎，再辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict urged him to hurry to court; he declined and was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue; he declined again and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was ordered to hurry to court. He declined and was made vice minister of revenue. He declined again but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 五年，改禮部侍郎，辭，詔不允，令所在州軍護遣至闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Vice Minister of Rites; he declined; an edict did not permit it and ordered the prefecture and army where he was to escort him to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made vice minister of rites. He declined, but the edict refused and ordered local authorities to escort him to court.

sentences.zh: 嵩之遣人謂詔曰：“毋言濟邸、宮媼、國本。”

translations.literal: Songzhi sent someone to tell Shao: "Do not speak of the Prince of Ji's residence, the palace wet-nurse, or the foundation of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi sent someone to tell Shao: "Do not speak of Prince Ji's case, the palace nurse, or the succession."

sentences.zh: 韶不答。

translations.literal: Shao did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shao made no reply.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：“臣生長淳熙初，猶及見度江盛時民生富樂，吏治修舉。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant grew up in early Chunxi and still caught sight of the flourishing time after crossing the river, when the people's lives were rich and joyful and official governance was well conducted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I grew up in early Chunxi and still remember the prosperity after the crossing of the Yangzi, when the people were content and governance was sound.

sentences.zh: 事變少異，政歸私門，紹定之末，元氣索矣。

translations.literal: When affairs changed slightly, government returned to private cliques; by the end of Shaoding, vital energy was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When troubles arose, power passed to private factions. By the end of Shaoding, the state's vital energy was spent.

sentences.zh: 端平更化，陛下初意豈不甚美。

translations.literal: In Duanping the polity was reformed; was not Your Majesty's original intent very fine?
translations.idiomatic: In the Duanping reforms, was not Your Majesty's original intent admirable?

sentences.zh: 國事日壞，其人或罷或死，莫有為陛下任其責者。

translations.literal: State affairs grow worse daily; those men are either dismissed or dead, and none bears responsibility for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs worsen daily. Those men are dismissed or dead, and none bears responsibility on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 考論至是，天下事豈非陛下所當自任而力為乎？

translations.literal: Considering matters to this point, are not the affairs of the realm what Your Majesty ought personally to undertake and strive for?
translations.idiomatic: When matters have come to this pass, should not Your Majesty personally shoulder the affairs of the realm and strive with all your strength?

sentences.zh: 《左氏》載史墨言：‘魯公世從其失，季氏世修其勤。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary records Shi Mo saying: "The Duke of Lu for generations followed his errors, while the Ji clan for generations cultivated its diligence."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary records Shi Mo saying: "The Duke of Lu for generations followed his errors, while the Ji clan for generations cultivated its diligence."

sentences.zh: ’蓋言所由來者漸矣。

translations.literal: This is to say that what comes has been gradual.
translations.idiomatic: This means that decline comes gradually.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦日久，宜深思熟念，威福自己，誰得而盜之哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ruled long; you ought to think deeply and reflect carefully—authority and blessing are your own; who can steal them?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned long. Think deeply: power and favor are yours alone—who can steal them?

sentences.zh: 舍此不為，悠悠玩悽，乃幾於《左氏》所謂‘世從其失者。

translations.literal: If you abandon this and do not act, idly playing and grieving, you are nearly what the Zuo Commentary calls "one who for generations follows his errors."
translations.idiomatic: If you abandon this and drift in idle grief, you will become nearly what the Zuo Commentary calls one who for generations follows his errors."

sentences.zh: ’”蓋以世卿風嵩之也。

translations.literal: This was aimed at the hereditary-minister style of Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: This was aimed at Songzhi's hereditary-minister style of power."

sentences.zh: 疏出，嵩之不悅，曰：“治《春秋》人下語毒”當是時，杜範亦在列，二人廉直，中外稱為“李、杜”。

translations.literal: When the memorial came out, Songzhi was displeased and said: "Men who study the Spring and Autumn Annals speak poisonously below." At that time Du Fan was also in the ranks; the two were incorrupt and upright, and inside and outside called them "Li and Du."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial appeared, Songzhi was displeased and said: "Men who study the Spring and Autumn speak poisonously." At that time Du Fan was also at court. The two were known for integrity, and court and country called them "Li and Du."

sentences.zh: 兼侍講，累辭，兼國史編修、實錄檢討，辭，遷吏部侍郎兼中書舍人，三辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was made concurrent Lecturer-in-Attendance and repeatedly declined; was made concurrent Compiler of the National History and Reviser of the Veritable Records and declined; was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently Drafting Secretary, declined three times, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made concurrent lecturer-in-attendance and repeatedly declined, then concurrent compiler of the National History and reviser of the Veritable Records, which he also declined. He was promoted to vice minister of personnel and drafting secretary, declined three times, and was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，疏言：“道揆之地，愛善類不勝於愛爵祿，畏公議不勝於畏權勢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou he memorialized saying: "In the post of chief minister, love of worthy men does not overcome love of rank and salary, and fear of public opinion does not overcome fear of power and influence.
translations.idiomatic: In 1242 he memorialized: "In the chief minister's post, love of worthy men does not outweigh love of rank and salary, and fear of public opinion does not outweigh fear of power.

sentences.zh: 陛下以腹心寄之大臣，大臣以腹心寄之一二都司，恐不能周天下之慮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty entrusts your innermost heart to the great ministers, and the great ministers entrust their innermost hearts to one or two bureau chiefs—I fear they cannot encompass the concerns of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty entrusts your innermost counsel to the chief ministers, and they entrust theirs to one or two bureau chiefs—I fear this cannot encompass the concerns of the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 故以之用人，則能用其所知，豈能用其所不知；

translations.literal: Therefore, using them to employ men, they can employ only those they know—how can they employ those they do not know?
translations.idiomatic: If they choose officials, they can appoint only those they know—how can they appoint those they do not know?

sentences.zh: 以之守法，則能守其所不與，必不能守於其所欲與。”

translations.literal: Using them to uphold law, they can uphold what they do not wish to grant but surely cannot uphold what they wish to grant."
translations.idiomatic: If they uphold the law, they can enforce what they do not wish to grant but cannot enforce what they wish to grant."

sentences.zh: 又及濟王、國本、宮媼。

translations.literal: He also touched on Prince Ji, the foundation of the state, and the palace wet-nurse.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of Prince Ji, the succession, and the palace nurse.

sentences.zh: 三上疏乞歸，以寶章閣直學士知泉州，辭，乞畀祠，不許。

translations.literal: He submitted three memorials begging to return home and was made Baozhang Pavilion Academician and prefect of Quanzhou; he declined and begged for a temple stipend; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials asking to retire and was appointed Baozhang Pavilion academician and prefect of Quanzhou. He declined and asked for a temple stipend, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 既歸，三辭，仍舊職提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: After returning, he declined three times and still held his former post as overseer of the Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he declined three times and retained his former post as overseer of the Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 淳祐五年，韶被召，再辭，詔本州通判勸勉赴闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunyou, Shao was summoned; he declined twice; an edict ordered the vice prefect of his prefecture to urge and encourage him to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1245 Shao was summoned. He declined twice, and an edict ordered the local vice prefect to urge him to court.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，三辭，遷權禮部尚書，復三辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, declined three times, was transferred to Acting Minister of Rites, declined three times again, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of rites and declined three times, then acting minister of rites and declined three times again, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 入見，疏曰：“陛下改畀正權，並進時望，天下孰不延頸以覬大治。

translations.literal: Entering audience, he memorialized saying: "Your Majesty has changed and entrusted correct authority, advancing men of the age's renown together—who under Heaven does not stretch his neck hoping for great order?
translations.idiomatic: At audience he memorialized: "Your Majesty has restored proper authority and advanced men of reputation. Who in the realm does not hope for great governance?

sentences.zh: 臣竊窺之，恐猶前日也。

translations.literal: Your servant secretly observes and fears it is still as the day before.
translations.idiomatic: I observe in secret and fear it is still as before.

sentences.zh: 君子小人，倫類不同。

translations.literal: The gentleman and the petty man belong to different categories of principle.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen and petty men belong to different orders of being.

sentences.zh: 惟不計近功，不急小利，然後君子有以自見；

translations.literal: Only if one does not calculate near-term achievement and does not hurry after small profit can the gentleman then have means to show himself;
translations.idiomatic: Only if you do not chase immediate results or petty profit can gentlemen make themselves known;

sentences.zh: 不惡聞過，不諱盡言，然後小人無以自托。

translations.literal: only if one does not hate hearing of faults and does not taboo full speech can petty men then have no means to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: only if you do not hate to hear of faults and do not suppress full speech can petty men find no foothold.

sentences.zh: 不然，治亂安危，反覆手爾。”

translations.literal: Otherwise, order and chaos, safety and peril, are but a turn of the hand."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, order and chaos, safety and peril, turn on a hand's reversal."

sentences.zh: 又曰：“陛下所謀者嬪妃近習，所信者貴戚近親。

translations.literal: He also said: "What Your Majesty consults are consorts and close attendants; whom Your Majesty trusts are noble kin and near relatives.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Your Majesty consults consorts and close attendants and trusts noble kin and near relatives.

sentences.zh: 按《政和令》：‘諸國戚、命婦若女冠、尼，不因大禮等輒求入內者，許臺諫覺察彈奏。

translations.literal: According to the Statutes of Zhenghe: "All imperial kin, titled ladies, female Taoists, and nuns who without great ritual or the like seek entry within are permitted to be detected and impeached by the censorial and remonstrating offices."
translations.idiomatic: According to the Statutes of Zhenghe: "Imperial kin, titled ladies, Taoist priestesses, and nuns who seek entry to the inner palace without proper ritual may be detected and impeached by the censorial offices."

sentences.zh: ’乞申嚴禁廷之籍，以絕天下之謗。

translations.literal: I beg that the forbidden-court register be strictly enforced to cut off slander throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the register of those forbidden the inner court be strictly enforced to end public criticism.

sentences.zh: 世臣貴戚，牽聯並進，何示人以不廣也。

translations.literal: Hereditary ministers and noble kin are advanced in linked groups—what does this show people about breadth?
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary ministers and noble kin advance in linked groups—what does this show about breadth of vision?

sentences.zh: 借曰以才選，他時萬一有非才者援是以求進，將何以抑之耶！”

translations.literal: Even if selection is by talent, if in future there should by any chance be one without talent who cites this to seek advancement, how will you suppress him!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if selection is by talent, when unworthy men cite this precedent to seek advancement, how will you refuse them?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：“今土地日蹙者未反，人民喪敗者未復，兵財止有此數，旦旦而理之，不過椎剝州縣，朘削裏閭。

translations.literal: He also said: "Today lands that shrink daily have not been recovered, people lost and ruined have not been restored; troops and wealth have only this fixed amount—managing them day by day is nothing but pounding and stripping the prefectures and counties, paring down village lanes.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Lands shrink daily and are not recovered; people are lost and not restored. Troops and revenue are finite—managing them day by day means only squeezing the prefectures and stripping the villages.

sentences.zh: 就使韓、白復生，桑、孔繼出，能為陛下強兵理財，何補治亂安危之數，徒使國家負不韙之名。

translations.literal: Even if Han Xin and Bai Qi were reborn, and Sang Hongyang and Kong Yan continued forth, able to strengthen troops and order finances for Your Majesty—what would it add to the reckoning of order, chaos, safety, and peril? It would only make the state bear the name of wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Han Xin and Bai Qi were reborn, and Sang Hongyang and Kong Yan returned, able to strengthen the army and manage finances—what would that add to the balance of order and chaos? It would only bring the state a bad name.

sentences.zh: 況議論紛然，賢者不過茍容而去，不肖者反因是以媒其身，忠言至計之不行，淺功末利之是計，此君子小人進退機括所系，何不思之甚也！”

translations.literal: Moreover, when discourse is in turmoil, worthy men can only comply superficially and leave, while unworthy men instead use this to advance themselves. Loyal words and supreme plans are not carried out; shallow achievement and petty profit are what is calculated—on this hinge the advance and retreat of gentlemen and petty men depend. How can you not think on this deeply!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when debate rages, worthy men comply superficially and leave, while unworthy men use the turmoil to advance. Loyal counsel goes unheeded while petty gains are pursued—on this hinges whether gentlemen or petty men prevail. How can you not think deeply on this?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：“聞之道路，德音每下，昆蟲草木鹹被潤澤，恩獨不及於一枯胔。

translations.literal: He also said: "Heard on the roads: whenever gracious edicts descend, insects and plants, grass and trees all receive moistening bounty—yet grace alone does not reach one withered corpse.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "It is said on the roads that whenever gracious edicts descend, even insects and plants receive bounty—yet grace alone does not reach one withered corpse.

sentences.zh: 威斷出，自公卿大夫莫敢後先，令獨不行於一老媼。

translations.literal: When authoritative decisions issue forth, from high ministers down none dares lag behind—yet orders alone do not apply to one old woman.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial authority is exercised, from ministers down none dares disobey—yet orders alone do not apply to one old woman.

sentences.zh: 小大之臣積勞受爵，皆得以延於世，而國儲君副，社稷所賴以靈長，獨不蚤計而豫定。”

translations.literal: Ministers great and small who accumulate merit receive ranks and all may extend their lines through generations—yet the heir to the state storehouse and assistant to the ruler, on whom the altars of soil and grain rely for enduring vitality, alone are not early planned and predetermined."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who accumulate merit receive ranks and extend their lines through generations—yet the heir apparent, on whom the dynasty relies for endurance, alone is not planned and settled in advance."

sentences.zh: 又疏乞還，不許。

translations.literal: He again memorialized begging to return; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized asking to retire; this was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 兼侍讀，三辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was made concurrent Reader-in-Attendance; he declined three times; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made concurrent reader-in-attendance and declined three times, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 又三疏乞歸。

translations.literal: He again submitted three memorials begging to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three more memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 時遊似以人望用，然有牽制之者，韶奏云：“人主職論一相而已，非其人不以輕授。

translations.literal: At the time You Si was employed for his public esteem, yet there were those who restrained him. Shao memorialized saying: "The ruler's duty is to discuss one chief minister only; if he is not the right man, do not lightly grant the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time You Si was appointed for his public reputation, yet others restrained him. Shao memorialized: "The ruler's duty is to appoint one chief minister; if he is not the right man, do not grant the post lightly.

sentences.zh: 始而授之，如不得已，既乃疑之，反使不得有所為，是豈專任責成之體哉！

translations.literal: At first you grant it as if you had no choice; then you doubt him and in turn make him unable to accomplish anything—is this the form of entrusting sole responsibility and completing the charge?
translations.idiomatic: At first you appoint him as if reluctantly, then you doubt him and prevent him from acting—is this how to entrust sole responsibility?

sentences.zh: 所言之事不必聽，所用之人不必從，疑畏憂沮，而權去之矣。”

translations.literal: What he speaks of need not be heard; whom he employs need not be followed—suspicion, fear, worry, and dejection, and authority has left him."
translations.idiomatic: What he says need not be heeded; whom he appoints need not be followed—filled with suspicion and fear, he loses his authority."

sentences.zh: 擢翰林學士兼知制誥、兼侍讀，不拜，詔不許，又三辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician, concurrently Drafting Edicts and concurrently Reader-in-Attendance; he did not accept the appointment; an edict did not permit refusal; he declined three times again; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician with concurrent duties drafting edicts and as reader-in-attendance. He refused to accept; an edict refused his refusal; he declined three times again and was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 嵩之服除，有向用之意，殿中侍御史章琰、正言李昂英、監察御史黃師雍論列嵩之甚峻，詔落職予祠。

translations.literal: When Songzhi's mourning period ended he had the intention of being employed again. Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Yan, Remonstrator Li Angying, and Investigating Censor Huang Shiyong discussed and listed Songzhi very sternly; an edict stripped his office and granted a temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: When Songzhi's mourning ended he sought reappointment. Censors Zhang Yan, Li Angying, and Huang Shiyong impeached him sternly, and an edict stripped his office and granted a temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 韶同從官抗疏曰：“臣等謹按《春秋》桓公五年書：‘蔡人、衛人、陳人從王伐鄭。

translations.literal: Shao together with attendant officials submitted a resisting memorial saying: "We respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals, fifth year of Duke Huan: "The people of Cai, the people of Wei, and the people of Chen followed the king in attacking Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Shao and his colleagues submitted a joint memorial: "We respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals, fifth year of Duke Huan: "The people of Cai, Wei, and Chen followed the king in attacking Zheng."

sentences.zh: ’春秋之初，無君無親者莫甚於鄭莊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period, none who lacked ruler and kin was worse than Duke Zhuang of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Spring and Autumn era, none who lacked ruler and kin exceeded Duke Zhuang of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 二百四十二年之經，未有雲‘王伐國’者，而書‘王’書‘伐’，以見鄭之無王，而天王所當聲罪以致討。

translations.literal: In the classic of two hundred forty-two years there is never said "the king attacked a state," yet it writes "king" and writes "attacked" to show that Zheng had no king and that the Son of Heaven ought to proclaim guilt and bring punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the classic of 242 years it never simply says "the king attacked a state," yet it writes "king" and "attacked" to show that Zheng had no king and that the Son of Heaven ought to proclaim guilt and punish.

sentences.zh: 未有書諸侯從王以伐者，而書三國從王伐鄭，又見諸侯莫從王以伐罪，而三國之微者獨至，不足伸天王之義，初不聞以其嘗為王卿士而薄其伐。

translations.literal: There is never written that feudal lords followed the king to attack, yet it writes that the three states followed the king in attacking Zheng—again showing that feudal lords did not follow the king to attack the guilty, while only the small of the three states came, insufficient to extend the Son of Heaven's righteousness; from the first it is not heard that because Zheng had once been the king's minister its attack was slighted.
translations.idiomatic: It never writes that feudal lords followed the king to attack, yet it writes that three states followed the king against Zheng—showing that lords did not follow the king to punish guilt, while only three small states came, insufficient to uphold the Son of Heaven's righteousness. It is never said that because Zheng had once served the king, the attack was slighted.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不能正奸臣之罪，其過不專在上，蓋大臣百執事不能輔天子以討有罪，皆《春秋》所不赦。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty cannot rectify the guilt of treacherous ministers; the fault is not solely above, for the great ministers and the hundred functionaries cannot assist the Son of Heaven in punishing the guilty—all are what the Spring and Autumn Annals does not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty cannot rectify the guilt of treacherous ministers. The fault is not yours alone—the chief ministers and officials cannot assist the Son of Heaven in punishing the guilty. All are unpardonable by the Spring and Autumn standard.

sentences.zh: 乞斷以《春秋》之義，亟賜裁處。”

translations.literal: We beg that you decide by the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals and quickly grant disposition."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that you decide by the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals and act at once."

sentences.zh: 詔嵩之勒令致仕。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Songzhi to retire under compulsion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Songzhi to retire under compulsion.

sentences.zh: 既而嵩之進觀文殿大學士，韶上疏爭之甚力。

translations.literal: Soon after, Songzhi was advanced to Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture; Shao memorialized against this very forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Songzhi was promoted to grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture. Shao memorialized against this with great force.

sentences.zh: 未幾，琰、昂英他有所論列，並罷言職。

translations.literal: Before long Yan and Angying discussed and listed other matters and were both dismissed from remonstrating posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yan and Angying raised other charges and were both dismissed from their remonstrating posts.

sentences.zh: 韶復上疏留之。

translations.literal: Shao again memorialized to retain them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao again memorialized asking that they be retained.

sentences.zh: 七年，韶十上疏丐去，以端明殿學士提舉玉隆宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shao submitted ten memorials begging to leave and was made Academician of the Duanming Hall and overseer of the Yulong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Shao submitted ten memorials asking to retire and was made academician of the Duanming Hall and overseer of the Yulong Palace.

sentences.zh: 時直學士院應亻繇、中書舍人趙汝騰拜疏留韶內祠，未報。

translations.literal: At the time Academician of the Hanlin Institute Ying You and Drafting Secretary Zhao Ruteng submitted memorials begging to retain Shao at an inner temple stipend; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hanlin academician Ying You and drafting secretary Zhao Ruteng memorialized asking to retain Shao at an inner temple stipend. There was no response.

sentences.zh: 韶陛辭，疏甚剴切，其略曰：“彼此相視，莫行其誌，而

translations.literal: Shao took leave at court; his memorial was very earnest and thorough. Its gist said: "Each looking at the other, none carries out his intent, yet
translations.idiomatic: Shao took leave at court in a memorial that was very earnest. Its gist said: "Each looking at the other, none carries out his intent, yet

sentences.zh: 剸裁庶政，品量人物，相與運於冥冥之中者，不得不他有人焉。

translations.literal: in cutting and judging the myriad affairs of government, appraising men, and operating together in hidden obscurity, there must be others.
translations.idiomatic: in cutting and judging government affairs, appraising men, and operating together in secret, there must be others.

sentences.zh: 是中書之手可束，而臺諫之口可鈐，朝廷之事所當力為，不可枚舉，皆莫有任其責者，甚非所以示四方、一體統。”

translations.literal: The hands of the Secretariat may be bound and the mouths of the censorial and remonstrating offices may be sealed; affairs of court that ought to be striven for cannot be enumerated one by one—none bears responsibility. This is very far from showing the four quarters and unifying the polity."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat's hands may be bound and the censors' mouths sealed. Affairs the court ought to pursue are beyond counting, yet none bears responsibility. This is far from showing the four quarters a unified polity."

sentences.zh: 改提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀，即出國門，力辭，道次三衢，詔趣受命，再辭，仍奉祠玉隆。

translations.literal: He was changed to overseer of the Wanshou Observatory and concurrently Reader-in-Attendance; he immediately left the capital gate, declined forcefully, and on the road stopped at Sanqu. An edict urged him to accept the appointment; he declined again and still held temple service at Yulong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made overseer of the Wanshou Observatory and concurrent reader-in-attendance. He left the capital at once and declined forcefully. At Sanqu on the road an edict urged him to accept; he declined again and still held temple service at Yulong.

sentences.zh: 八年，被召，辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned; he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was summoned. He declined but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 再辭，仍舊職奉祠萬壽兼侍讀，令守臣以禮趣行。

translations.literal: He declined again and still held his former post, serving at the Wanshou temple stipend and concurrently as Reader-in-Attendance; local officials were ordered to urge him on his way with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He declined again and retained his former post at the Wanshou temple stipend with concurrent duties as reader-in-attendance. Local officials were ordered to urge him on his way with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又辭，不許。

translations.literal: He declined again; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined again but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 九年，仍奉祠玉隆。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he still held temple service at Yulong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he continued to hold temple service at Yulong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，祠滿再任。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when his temple stipend term was complete, he was reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when his temple stipend term expired, he was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 韶忠厚純實，平粹簡淡，不溺於聲色貨利，默坐一室，門無雜賓雲。

translations.literal: Shao was loyal, generous, pure, and sincere, level and clear, simple and plain, not drowning in sound, color, goods, or profit; he would sit silently in one room, and his gate had no miscellaneous guests.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was loyal, sincere, plain, and unpretentious, untempted by pleasure or profit. He would sit alone in his study, and no unworthy guest crossed his threshold.

sentences.zh: 王邁字貫之，興化軍仙遊人。

translations.literal: Wang Mai, courtesy name Guanzhi, was a native of Xianyou in Xinghua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mai, whose courtesy name was Guanzhi, came from Xianyou in Xinghua Commandery.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年進士，為潭州觀察推官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination and served as investigating officer of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1217 and served as investigating officer in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，調浙西安撫司幹官。

translations.literal: When his father died he was transferred as staff officer of the Zhexi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he was transferred as a staff officer of the Zhexi Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 考廷試，詳定官王元春欲私所親置高第，邁顯擿其繆，元春怒，嗾諫官李知孝誣邁在殿廬語聲高，免官。

translations.literal: During the palace examination, the grading official Wang Yuanchun wished to place a favorite in a high rank for private reasons; Mai openly exposed his error. Yuanchun was angry and incited remonstrator Li Zhixiao to accuse Mai of speaking loudly in the examination hall; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: During the palace examination, grading official Wang Yuanchun tried to place a favorite in a high rank. Mai exposed the fraud openly. Yuanchun incited remonstrator Li Zhixiao to accuse Mai of speaking loudly in the examination hall, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 調南外睦宗院教授。

translations.literal: He was transferred as professor of the Outer Muzong Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at the Outer Muzong Academy.

sentences.zh: 真德秀方守福州，邁竭忠以裨郡政。
