translations.literal: When Zhen Dexiu was governing Fuzhou, Mai exhausted his loyalty to assist prefectural administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen Dexiu governed Fuzhou, Mai served him loyally and assisted in prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 赴都堂審察，丞相鄭清之曰：“學官掌故，不足凂吾貫之。”

translations.literal: Going to the capital for court review, Chief Councillor Zheng Qingzhi said: "A school officer handling precedents is not enough to defile our Guanzhi."
translations.idiomatic: At court review, Chief Councillor Zheng Qingzhi said: "A mere school officer handling precedents is not fit for our Guanzhi."

sentences.zh: 俄召試學士院，策以楮幣，邁援據古今，考究本末，謂：“國貧楮多，弊始於兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned for examination at the Hanlin Institute, with paper currency as the topic. Mai cited ancient and modern cases and examined root and branch, saying: "The state is poor and paper notes are many; the abuse begins with war.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was examined at the Hanlin Institute on the topic of paper currency. Mai cited ancient and modern precedents and traced cause and effect, saying: "The state is poor and paper notes proliferate because the abuse begins with war.

sentences.zh: 乾、淳初行楮幣，止二千萬，時南北方休息也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiandao and Chunxi, paper currency issued amounted to only twenty million, when north and south were at rest.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qiandao and Chunxi reigns, paper currency in circulation was only twenty million, when north and south were at peace.

sentences.zh: 開禧兵興，增至一億四千萬矣。

translations.literal: When war arose in Kaixi, it increased to one hundred forty million.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in the Kaixi era, it rose to 140 million.

sentences.zh: 紹定有事山東，增至二億九千萬矣。

translations.literal: When Shaoding had affairs in Shandong, it increased to two hundred ninety million.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoding campaigns in Shandong followed, it rose to 290 million.

sentences.zh: 議者徒患楮窮，而弗懲兵禍，姑以今之尺籍校之，嘉定增至二十八萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: Discussants only worry that paper is exhausted and do not punish the calamity of war. For the moment, comparing with today's military registers, in Jiading it increased to two hundred eighty-eight thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Critics worry only that paper currency is exhausted and do not address the calamity of war. Compare today's military registers: by Jiading they had risen to over 288,000.

sentences.zh: 用寡謀之人，試直突之說，能發而不能收，能取而不能守。

translations.literal: Employing men of little counsel, testing the theory of direct assault—they can launch but cannot withdraw, can seize but cannot hold.
translations.idiomatic: Employing men of little counsel and testing theories of direct assault, they can launch but not withdraw, seize but not hold.

sentences.zh: 今無他策，核軍實，窒邊釁，救楮幣第一義也。”

translations.literal: Now there is no other strategy: verify military strength, stop frontier provocations—rescuing paper currency is the first principle."
translations.idiomatic: There is no other strategy now: verify military strength, stop frontier provocations, and rescue paper currency as the first priority."

sentences.zh: 又言：“修內司營繕廣，內帑宣索多，厚施緇黃，濫予嬪禦，若此未嘗裁撙，徒聞有括田、榷鹽之議者。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Inner Service Office's repairs are extensive, the inner treasury's requisitions are many, thick gifts are given to monks, and consorts and attendants are lavished with grants—such things have never been cut back, while one only hears talk of land confiscation and salt monopolies.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The Inner Service Office spends lavishly on repairs, the inner treasury demands endlessly, monks and palace women receive generous grants—yet such spending is never cut, while we hear only talk of land confiscation and salt monopolies.

sentences.zh: 向使二事可行，故相行之久矣。

translations.literal: If these two measures had been feasible, the former chief councillor would long ago have carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: If those two measures had worked, the former chief councillor would have adopted them long ago.

sentences.zh: 更化伊始，奈何取前日所不屑行者而行之乎？”

translations.literal: The reform has only just begun—why take up what you disdained the day before?"
translations.idiomatic: The reform has only just begun—why adopt what you disdained only yesterday?"

sentences.zh: 又因楮以及時事，言：“君子之類雖進，而其道未行；

translations.literal: He also extended from paper currency to current affairs, saying: "Men of the gentlemanly sort are advanced, yet their way is not carried out;
translations.idiomatic: He extended his argument to current affairs: "Men of the gentlemanly sort are advanced, yet their way is not followed;

sentences.zh: 小人之跡雖屏，而其心未服。”

translations.literal: the traces of petty men are removed, yet their hearts are not subdued."
translations.idiomatic: petty men are removed from office, yet their hearts are not subdued."

sentences.zh: 真德秀病危，聞邁所對，善之。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu was gravely ill; hearing Mai's responses, he approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu was gravely ill. When he heard Mai's answers, he approved of them.

sentences.zh: 帝再相喬行簡，或傳史嵩之復用，邁上封事曰：“天下之相，不與天下共謀之，是必冥冥之中有為之地者。

translations.literal: The emperor again made Qiao Xingjian chief councillor; some reported that Shi Songzhi would be employed again. Mai submitted a sealed memorial saying: "The chief minister of the realm does not deliberate with the realm—there must be someone acting in hidden obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again appointed Qiao Xingjian chief councillor. Rumors spread that Shi Songzhi would return. Mai submitted a sealed memorial: "The realm's chief minister does not deliberate with the realm—someone must be acting in the shadows.

sentences.zh: 且舊相奸憸刻薄，天下所知，復用，則君子空於一網矣。”

translations.literal: Moreover, the former chief councillor was treacherous, crafty, and harsh—known to all under Heaven. If he is employed again, gentlemen will be emptied into one net."
translations.idiomatic: The former chief councillor was treacherous and harsh, as all know. If he returns, every upright man will be caught in one net."

sentences.zh: 又言吳知古、陳洵益撓政。

translations.literal: He also spoke of Wu Zhigu and Chen Xunyi obstructing government.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of Wu Zhigu and Chen Xunyi obstructing government.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：“君不可欺天，臣不可欺君，厚權臣而薄同氣，為欺天之著。”

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he said: "The ruler cannot deceive Heaven; the minister cannot deceive the ruler. Honoring powerful ministers while slighting those of the same blood is a manifest deception of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said: "A ruler cannot deceive Heaven; a minister cannot deceive his ruler. Honoring powerful ministers while slighting kin of the same blood is a manifest deception of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 邁由疏遠見帝，空臆無隱，帝為改容。

translations.literal: Mai, from a distant post, saw the emperor, emptied his breast without concealment, and the emperor changed countenance for him.
translations.idiomatic: Mai, though from a distant post, spoke to the emperor without reserve, and the emperor's expression changed.

sentences.zh: 言者劾邁論邊事過實，魏了翁侍經筵，為帝言惜其去，改通判漳州。

translations.literal: Remonstrators impeached Mai for discussing frontier affairs beyond the facts. Wei Liaoweng attended the classics lecture and told the emperor he regretted Mai's departure; he was changed to vice prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics impeached Mai for overstating frontier affairs. Wei Liaoweng, attending the classics lecture, told the emperor he regretted losing Mai. Mai was made vice prefect of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 禋祀雷雨，邁應詔言：“天與寧考之怒久矣。

translations.literal: During suburban sacrifice there was thunder and rain. Mai responded to an edict saying: "Heaven and the late Emperor Ning have been angry for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: During suburban sacrifice, thunder and rain struck. Mai responded to an edict: "Heaven and the late Emperor Ning have long been angry.

sentences.zh: 曲糵致疾，妖冶伐性，初秋逾旬，曠不視事，道路憂疑，此天與寧考之所以怒也。

translations.literal: Wine and brew cause illness; seductive beauty erodes one's nature. In early autumn for more than ten days you have neglected affairs; the roads are full of worry and doubt—this is why Heaven and the late Emperor Ning are angry.
translations.idiomatic: Wine causes illness; seductive beauty erodes the nature. For more than ten days in early autumn you have neglected affairs, and the people are anxious—this is why Heaven and the late Emperor Ning are angry.

sentences.zh: 隱、刺覆絕，攸、熹尊寵，綱淪法斁，上行下效，京卒外兵，狂悖叠起，此天與寧考之所以怒也。

translations.literal: Yin and Ci were overthrown and extinguished; You and Xi were honored and favored; the net was lost and law decayed; above acted and below imitated; capital soldiers and outer troops rose in mad rebellion one upon another—this is why Heaven and the late Emperor Ning are angry.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Ci were destroyed; You and Xi were favored; law and order collapsed; example spread from above to below; capital and frontier troops rebelled in succession—this is why Heaven and the late Emperor Ning are angry.

sentences.zh: 陛下不是之思，方用漢災異免三公故事，環顧在廷，莫知所付。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not reflect on these faults but is just now using the Han precedent of dismissing the Three Excellencies because of omens, looking around those at court without knowing whom to entrust.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not reflect on these faults but follows the Han precedent of dismissing the Three Excellencies because of omens, looking around the court without knowing whom to trust.

sentences.zh: 遙相崔與之，臣恐與之不至，政柄他有所屬，此世道否泰，君子小人進退之機也。”

translations.literal: You summon Cui Yuzhi from afar—I fear Yuzhi will not come, and governmental authority will belong elsewhere. On this hinges whether the age turns prosperous or adverse, and whether gentlemen and petty men advance or retreat."
translations.idiomatic: You summon Cui Yuzhi from afar—I fear he will not come and power will belong elsewhere. On this hinges whether the age prospers or declines, and whether gentlemen or petty men prevail."

sentences.zh: 於是臺官李大同言邁交結德秀、了翁及洪咨夔以收虛譽，削一秩免。

translations.literal: Thereupon censor Li Datong said Mai had associated with Dexiu, Liaoweng, and Hong Zikui to gather empty reputation; one rank was stripped and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Datong charged that Mai had cultivated Dexiu, Liaoweng, and Hong Zikui to win empty reputation. One rank was stripped and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 蔣峴劾邁前疏妄論倫紀，請坐以非所宜言之罪，削二秩。

translations.literal: Jiang Xian impeached Mai's earlier memorial for rashly discussing human relations and ritual order and asked that he be punished for speaking what ought not to be spoken; two ranks were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xian impeached Mai's earlier memorial for rashly discussing ritual order and asked that he be punished for improper speech; two ranks were stripped.

sentences.zh: 久之，復通判贛州，改福州、建康府、信州，皆不行。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again made vice prefect of Ganzhou; he was changed to Fuzhou, Jiankang Prefecture, and Xinzhou, but took none of these posts.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again made vice prefect of Ganzhou and was reassigned to Fuzhou, Jiankang, and Xinzhou, but accepted none of these posts.

sentences.zh: 淳祐改元，通判吉州。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Chunyou he was vice prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chunyou era he served as vice prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 右正言江萬里袖疏榻前曰：“邁之才可惜，不即召，將有老不及之嘆。”

translations.literal: Right Remonstrator Jiang Wanli placed a memorial in his sleeve before the throne and said: "Mai's talent is regrettable to waste; if he is not summoned at once, there will be the sigh that he grew old before it could be used."
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrator Jiang Wanli presented a memorial at the throne: "Mai's talent is too valuable to waste. If he is not summoned soon, we will sigh that he grew old before it could be used."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 有尼之者，遂止。

translations.literal: There were those who obstructed it, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Someone obstructed it, and the matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 知邵武軍。

translations.literal: He governed Shaowu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Shaowu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 在郡，詔以亢旱求言，邁驛奏七事，而以徹龍翔宮、立濟王後為先。

translations.literal: In the commandery, an edict because of severe drought sought remonstrance; Mai submitted by post relay seven matters, putting first the abolition of the Longxiang Palace and the establishment of an heir to Prince Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery, an edict because of drought sought advice. Mai submitted seven matters by post, putting first the abolition of the Longxiang Palace and the establishment of an heir to Prince Ji.

sentences.zh: 時鄭清之再相，以左司郎官召，力辭。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Qingzhi was again chief councillor; Mai was summoned as Left Office Registrar and declined forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Qingzhi was again chief councillor, Mai was summoned as Left Office registrar and declined forcefully.

sentences.zh: 以直秘閣提點廣東刑獄，亦辭，改侍右郎官，諫官焦炳炎論罷。

translations.literal: He was made Direct Secretarial Pavilion Associate and intendant of Guangdong judicial affairs; he also declined. He was changed to Attendant of the Right Office; remonstrator Jiao Bingyan discussed and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Secretarial Pavilion associate and intendant of Guangdong judicial affairs and declined. He was made attendant of the Right Office; remonstrator Jiao Bingyan had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 予祠，卒，贈司農少卿。

translations.literal: He was granted a temple stipend, died, and was posthumously granted Vice Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a temple stipend, died, and was posthumously honored as Vice Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 邁以學問詞章發身，尤練世務。

translations.literal: Mai rose through learning and literary composition and was especially practiced in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mai rose through learning and literary accomplishment and was especially skilled in practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 易祓戒潭人曰：“此君不可犯。”

translations.literal: Yi Fu warned the people of Tanzhou saying: "This gentleman cannot be provoked."
translations.idiomatic: Yi Fu warned the people of Tanzhou: "This man cannot be provoked."

sentences.zh: 奪勢家冒占田數百畝以還民。

translations.literal: He seized several hundred mu of land that powerful families had falsely occupied and returned it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed several hundred mu of land that powerful families had illegally occupied and returned it to the people.

sentences.zh: 李宗勉嘗論邁，然邁評近世宰輔，至宗勉，必曰“賢相”。

translations.literal: Li Zongmian once criticized Mai, yet when Mai evaluated recent chief ministers, reaching Zongmian he always said "worthy chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmian once criticized Mai, yet when Mai evaluated recent chief ministers, he always called Zongmian a worthy chief minister.

sentences.zh: 徐清叟與邁有違言，邁晚應詔，謂清叟有人望可用。

translations.literal: Xu Qingsou and Mai had words of disagreement; in his later response to an edict, Mai said Qingsou had public esteem and could be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qingsou and Mai had disagreed, but in a later memorial Mai said Qingsou had public esteem and could be employed.

sentences.zh: 世服其公云。

translations.literal: The age admired his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The world admired his fairness.

sentences.zh: 史彌鞏，字南叔，彌遠從弟也。

translations.literal: Shi Migong, courtesy name Nanshu, was a younger cousin of Miyuan on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Migong, whose courtesy name was Nanshu, was a younger cousin of Shi Miyuan.

sentences.zh: 好學強記。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had a strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had a remarkable memory.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年，入太學，升上舍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi he entered the Imperial College and was promoted to the upper dormitory.
translations.idiomatic: In 1193 he entered the Imperial College and was promoted to the upper dormitory.

sentences.zh: 時彌遠柄國，寄理不獲試，淹抑十載。

translations.literal: At the time Miyuan held the state; Migong's deferred examination was not granted, and he was held back for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: While Miyuan held power, Migong's deferred examination was denied and he was held back for ten years.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年，始登進士第。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading he at last passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1217 he finally received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 時李埴開鄂閫，知彌鞏持論不阿，辟咨幕府事。

translations.literal: At the time Li [damaged character] opened the Ezhou command; knowing that Migong held to his views without bending, he recruited him to consult on headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander of the Ezhou defense opened his headquarters, knowing Migong would not bend his principles, he recruited him as a staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 壽昌戍卒失律，欲盡誅其亂者，乃請誅倡者一人，軍心感服。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers at Shouchang violated discipline; the commander wished to execute all the mutineers. Migong asked that only the ringleader be executed, and army hearts were moved to submission.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison soldiers at Shouchang mutinied, the commander wished to execute them all. Migong asked that only the ringleader be put to death, and the troops submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 改知溧水縣，首嚴庠序之教。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Lishui County and first made strict the teaching of the schools.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Lishui County and made strict education in the local schools his first priority.

sentences.zh: 端平初，入監都進奏院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping he entered service overseeing the Court of Imperial Memorials.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duanping era he entered service at the Court of Imperial Memorials.

sentences.zh: 轉對，有君子小人才不才之奏，護蜀保江之奏。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he submitted memorials on gentlemen and petty men, talent and lack of talent, and on protecting Shu and securing the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he submitted memorials distinguishing gentlemen from petty men and talent from mediocrity, and on protecting Sichuan and securing the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，都城火，彌鞏應詔上書，謂修省之未至者有五。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi the capital caught fire; Migong responded to an edict with a memorial saying there were five things in self-cultivation and restraint not yet attained.
translations.idiomatic: In 1237, when fire struck the capital, Migong responded to an edict with a memorial listing five failures of self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“天倫之變，世孰無之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Changes in human relations—who in the age lacks them?
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Changes in family bonds—who in this age lacks them?

sentences.zh: 陛下友愛之心亦每發見。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart of brotherly love also appears from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart of brotherly love also appears from time to time.

sentences.zh: 洪咨夔所以蒙陛下殊知者，謂霅川之變非濟邸之本心，濟邸之死非陛下之本心，其言深有以契聖心耳，矧以先帝之子，陛下之兄，乃使不能安其體魄於地下，豈不幹和氣，召災異乎？

translations.literal: The reason Hong Zikui received Your Majesty's special trust was that he said the upheaval at Zechuan was not Prince Ji's original intent, and Prince Ji's death was not Your Majesty's original intent—his words deeply matched the sage heart. How much more, then, since he was the late emperor's son and Your Majesty's elder brother, to make him unable to rest his body and soul underground—does this not disturb harmonious qi and summon omens and anomalies?
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zikui won Your Majesty's special trust because he said the upheaval at Zechuan was not Prince Ji's intent and Prince Ji's death was not Your Majesty's intent—words that deeply matched the imperial heart. Yet he was the late emperor's son and Your Majesty's elder brother—can he not rest in peace underground? Does this not disturb harmony and summon omens?

sentences.zh: 蒙蔽把握，良有以也。”

translations.literal: Obstruction and control—there are indeed reasons for it."
translations.idiomatic: There are indeed reasons for such obstruction and control."

sentences.zh: 出提點江東刑獄。

translations.literal: He went out as intendant of Jiangdong judicial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed intendant of Jiangdong judicial affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，饒、信、南康三郡大侵，謂振荒在得人，俾厘戶為五，甲乙以等第振糶，丙為自給，丁糴而戊濟，全活為口一百一十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: The year suffered great drought; Rao, Xin, and Nankang commanderies were greatly afflicted. He said that famine relief lay in obtaining the right men, had households sorted into five categories, used grades A and B for graded grain sales, C for self-sufficiency, D for purchase and E for relief, and preserved alive more than 1,140,000 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe drought, Rao, Xin, and Nankang suffered greatly. He held that famine relief depended on the right men. He classified households into five grades: A and B received graded grain sales, C were self-sufficient, D purchased grain, and E received relief. More than 1,140,000 lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 徽之休寧有淮民三十餘輩，操戈劫人財，逮捕，法曹以不傷人論罪。

translations.literal: In Xiuzhou, Huining, more than thirty Huai migrants took up weapons and robbed people's property. When arrested, the legal office judged the crime on the ground that no one was injured.
translations.idiomatic: In Huining, Xiuzhou, more than thirty Huai migrants armed themselves and robbed travelers. When arrested, the legal office judged them leniently because no one was injured.

sentences.zh: 彌鞏曰：“持兵為盜，貸之，是滋盜也。”

translations.literal: Migong said: "Bearing weapons to rob—if you pardon them, you nourish bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Migong said: "Armed robbery—if you pardon it, you encourage banditry."

sentences.zh: 推情重者僇數人，一道以寧。

translations.literal: He punished several of the gravest cases, and the whole circuit was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He executed several of the worst offenders, and the whole circuit was pacified.

sentences.zh: 饒州兵籍溢數，供億不繼，請汰冗兵。

translations.literal: Raozhou's military registers exceeded the quota and supplies could not keep up; he requested reduction of redundant troops.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou's military rolls exceeded the quota and supplies could not keep up. He requested reduction of redundant troops.

sentences.zh: 令下，營門大噪。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, the camp gates erupted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When the order was issued, the camps erupted in uproar.

sentences.zh: 乃呼諸校謂曰：“汰不當，許自陳，敢嘩者斬。”

translations.literal: He then summoned the commanders and said: "If the reduction is wrong, you may state it yourselves; whoever dares make an uproar will be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the commanders and said: "If the reduction is unjust, you may appeal. Whoever makes an uproar will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 鹹叩頭請罪，諸營帖然，稟給亦大省。

translations.literal: All kowtowed and begged forgiveness; every camp became orderly, and grain distributions were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: All kowtowed and begged forgiveness. Every camp became orderly, and grain distributions were greatly reduced.

sentences.zh: 召為司封郎中，以兄子嵩之入相，引嫌丐祠，遂以直華文閣知婺州。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Registrar in the Bureau of Audience; because his elder brother's son Songzhi entered the chief ministership, he cited conflict of interest and begged a temple stipend, and was then made Direct Huawen Pavilion Academician and prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as registrar in the Bureau of Audience. When his nephew Songzhi became chief councillor, he cited conflict of interest and sought a temple stipend, then was made Direct Huawen Pavilion academician and prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時年已七十，丐祠，提舉崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He was already seventy and begged a temple stipend as overseer of the Chongxi Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he sought a temple stipend and was made overseer of the Chongxi Observatory.

sentences.zh: 里居絕口不道時事。

translations.literal: Living at home, he never spoke of current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he never spoke of current affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 真德秀嘗曰：史南叔不登宗袞之門者三十年，未仕則為其寄理，已仕則為其排擯，爵然不汙有如此。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu once said: Shi Nanshu did not enter the clan registry's door for thirty years—before office he was blocked by deferred examination, after office he was pushed aside—yet he remained lofty and unstained to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu once said: Shi Nanshu did not enter the clan registry's door for thirty years—blocked from examination before office, pushed aside after office—yet he remained lofty and unstained.

sentences.zh: 五子，長肯之，終刑部郎官，能之、有之、胄之俱進士。

translations.literal: He had five sons. The eldest, Kenzhi, ended as Registrar in the Ministry of Justice; Nengzhi, Youzhi, and Zhouzhi all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons. The eldest, Kenzhi, became registrar in the Ministry of Justice; Nengzhi, Youzhi, and Zhouzhi all received jinshi degrees.

sentences.zh: 肯之子蒙卿，鹹淳元年進士，調江陰軍教授，蚤受業色川陽恪，為學淹博，著書立言，一以朱熹為法。

translations.literal: Kenzhi's son Mengqing passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Xianchun, was assigned professor of Jiangyin Commandery, early studied under Yang Ke of Sechuan, was broad in learning, wrote books and established doctrines, and took Zhu Xi alone as his model.
translations.idiomatic: Kenzhi's son Mengqing received his jinshi degree in 1265 and was appointed professor at Jiangyin Commandery. He had studied early under Yang Ke of Sechuan, was learned and prolific, and took Zhu Xi alone as his model.

sentences.zh: 陳塤，字和仲，慶元府鄞人。

translations.literal: Chen Xun, courtesy name Hezhong, was a native of Yin in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun, whose courtesy name was Hezhong, came from Yin in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大父叔平與同郡樓鑰友善，死，鑰哭之。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuping was friendly with Lou Yue of the same commandery; when he died, Yue wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuping was a friend of Lou Yue of the same district. When Shuping died, Yue wept for him.

sentences.zh: 塤才四歲，出揖如成人。

translations.literal: Xun was only four; he came out and bowed like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was only four years old but came out and bowed like an adult.

sentences.zh: 鑰指盤中銀杏使屬對，塤應聲曰：“金桃。”

translations.literal: Yue pointed to the ginkgo in the dish and told him to make a parallel; Xun answered on the spot: "Golden peach."
translations.idiomatic: Yue pointed to the ginkgo on the dish and asked for a parallel couplet. Xun answered instantly: "Golden peach."

sentences.zh: 問何所據？

translations.literal: Asked on what basis?
translations.idiomatic: Asked what his basis was,

sentences.zh: 對以杜詩“鸚鵡啄金桃。”

translations.literal: he answered with Du Fu's line "The parrot pecks the golden peach."
translations.idiomatic: he cited Du Fu's line, "The parrot pecks the golden peach."

sentences.zh: 鑰竦然曰：“亡友不死矣。”

translations.literal: Yue was startled and said: "My dead friend is not dead after all."
translations.idiomatic: Yue exclaimed in wonder: "My dead friend lives again."

sentences.zh: 長受《周官》於劉著，頃刻數千百言輒就。

translations.literal: Growing up, he studied the Offices of Zhou under Liu Zhuo and could complete several thousand or hundred words in a moment.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew, he studied the Offices of Zhou under Liu Zhuo and could compose thousands of words in moments.

sentences.zh: 試江東轉運司第一，試禮部復為第一。

translations.literal: In the Jiangdong Transport Commission examination he placed first; in the Ministry of Rites examination he again placed first.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the Jiangdong Transport Commission examination and first again in the Ministry of Rites examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年，登進士第。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1217 he received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 調黃州教授。

translations.literal: He was assigned professor of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 喪父毀瘠，考古禮制時祭、儀制、祭器行之。

translations.literal: When his father died he was emaciated by mourning; he investigated ancient ritual regulations and put seasonal sacrifices, ceremonial regulations, and sacrificial vessels into practice.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned until emaciated, researched ancient ritual regulations, and put seasonal sacrifices, ceremonial rules, and sacrificial vessels into practice.

sentences.zh: 忽嘆曰：“俗學不足學。”

translations.literal: Suddenly he sighed and said: "Vulgar learning is not worth studying."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he sighed: "Vulgar learning is not worth studying."

sentences.zh: 乃師事楊簡，攻苦食淡，晝夜不怠。

translations.literal: He then took Yang Jian as his teacher, toiled bitterly and ate plainly, and did not slacken day or night.
translations.idiomatic: He then studied under Yang Jian, living in hardship and plain fare, working day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 免喪，史彌遠當國，謂之曰：“省元魁數千人，狀元魁百人，而恩數逾等，盍令省元初授堂除教授，當自君始。”

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Shi Miyuan held the state and said to him: "Provincial top graduates number several thousand, palace top graduates number a hundred, yet favor exceeds its proper grade—why not let provincial top graduates at first receive direct court appointment as professors? It should begin with you."
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Shi Miyuan held power and told him: "Provincial top graduates number in the thousands and palace top graduates in the hundreds, yet favor exceeds proper rank. Let provincial top graduates receive direct court appointment as professors first—it should begin with you."

sentences.zh: 塤謝曰：“廟堂之議甚盛，舉自塤始，得無嫌乎？”

translations.literal: Chen Xun declined and said: "The deliberations at court run very high; if the initiative begins with Xun, will there not be grounds for suspicion?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun declined: "Court deliberations are already charged enough—if the proposal starts with me, will that not invite resentment?"

sentences.zh: 徑部註處州教授以去，士論高之。

translations.literal: He directly had the ministry register him as professor at Chuzhou and departed; scholarly opinion held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He had the ministry assign him directly as professor at Chuzhou and left his post; scholars everywhere praised him.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，詔求言，塤上封事曰：“上有憂危之心，下有安泰之象，世道之所由隆。

translations.literal: When Lizong ascended the throne, an edict sought advice. Xun submitted a sealed memorial saying: "When those above harbor hearts of worry and peril while those below show signs of peace and security, that is how the age rises.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, the court called for memorials. Chen Xun submitted a sealed petition: "When rulers above feel worry and peril while the realm below appears secure, the age flourishes.

sentences.zh: 上有安泰之心，下有憂危之象，世道之所由汙。

translations.literal: When those above harbor hearts of peace and security while those below show signs of worry and peril, that is how the age is defiled.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers above feel secure while the realm below shows signs of distress, the age decays.

sentences.zh: 故為天下而憂，則樂隨之。

translations.literal: Therefore one who worries for the realm will find joy follow in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, worry for the realm brings joy in its wake.

sentences.zh: 以天下為樂，則憂隨之。

translations.literal: One who takes the realm as a source of joy will find worry follow in turn.
translations.idiomatic: But treat the realm as a source of pleasure, and worry follows.

sentences.zh: 有天下者，在乎善審憂樂之機而已。

translations.literal: One who holds the realm depends on properly discerning the pivot between worry and joy—nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds the realm must learn to read the balance between worry and complacency—that is all.

sentences.zh: 今日之敝，莫大於人心之不合，紀綱之不振，風俗之不淳，國敝人偷而不可救。

translations.literal: The ills of today are greatest in hearts not united, statutes not enforced, customs not pure—the state decayed, the people lax, beyond rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Today's worst ills are disunity of heart, lax discipline, and corrupt custom—the state enfeebled, the people slack, seemingly beyond saving.

sentences.zh: 願陛下養之以正，勵之以實，蒞之以明，斷之以武。”

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will nourish with rectitude, spur with substance, attend with clarity, and decide with firmness."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty cultivate the realm with righteousness, drive it with earnest effort, govern with clear sight, and rule with resolute force."

sentences.zh: 而塤直聲始著於天下。

translations.literal: And Xun's reputation for forthright speech began to become known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From this point Chen Xun's reputation for blunt honesty spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 與郡守高似孫不合，去，歸奉其母。

translations.literal: He did not get along with the prefect Gao Sisun, resigned, and returned home to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with the prefect Gao Sisun, left office, and went home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 召為太學錄，逾年始至。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Recorder of the Imperial College; more than a year passed before he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to serve as Recorder of the Imperial College, he did not arrive for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 轉對，言：“天道無親，民心難保。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he said: "Heaven's way favors no one; the hearts of the people are hard to keep.
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating audience he warned: "Heaven shows no partiality; the loyalty of the people is hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 日月逾邁，事會莫留。

translations.literal: Days and months pass beyond recall; occasions for action do not wait.
translations.idiomatic: Days and months slip away; decisive moments will not linger.

sentences.zh: 始之銳，久則怠。

translations.literal: At first keen, over time slack.
translations.idiomatic: Vigor at the start gives way to slackness in time.

sentences.zh: 始之明，久則昏。

translations.literal: At first clear, over time dim.
translations.idiomatic: Clarity at the start gives way to confusion in time.

sentences.zh: 垂拱仰成，盛心也，不可因以負有為之誌。

translations.literal: To sit with folded hands and rely on others to complete affairs is a generous mind, but one must not use it as a reason to abandon resolve for action.
translations.idiomatic: To rule at ease while others do the work shows a generous spirit—but that must not become an excuse to abandon the will to act.

sentences.zh: 遵養時晦，至德也，不可因以失乘時之機。”

translations.literal: To nourish virtue and bide one's time in obscurity is supreme virtue, but one must not use it as a reason to miss the moment when opportunity comes."
translations.idiomatic: To cultivate virtue and wait for the right hour is the highest conduct—but that must not become an excuse to miss the hour when it arrives."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the memorial and adopted its counsel.

sentences.zh: 遷太學博士，主宗正寺簿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Doctor of the Imperial College and served as chief registrar of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Doctor of the Imperial College, he also served as chief registrar of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 都城火，塤步往玉牒所，盡藏玉牒於石室。

translations.literal: When the capital caught fire, Xun walked to the imperial genealogy office and stored all the genealogical registers in a stone vault.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out in the capital, Chen Xun went on foot to the imperial genealogy office and hid every register in a stone chamber.

sentences.zh: 詔遷官，不受。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his promotion; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered him promoted; he refused.

sentences.zh: 應詔言應上天非常之怒者，當有非常之舉動，歷陳致災之由。

translations.literal: Responding to an imperial summons he said that extraordinary wrath from Heaven above requires extraordinary action, and he enumerated in detail the causes of the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Answering an imperial summons, he argued that Heaven's extraordinary anger demands extraordinary measures, and laid out at length what had brought the disaster about.

sentences.zh: 又有吳潛、汪泰亨上彌遠書，乞正馮榯、王虎不盡力救火之罪，及行知臨安府林介、兩浙轉運使趙汝憚之罰。

translations.literal: Wu Qian and Wang Taiheng also submitted a letter to Miyuan, requesting punishment for Feng Rong and Wang Hu for not exerting themselves fully to fight the fire, and penalties for Lin Jie, acting prefect of Lin'an, and Zhao Rudan, transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qian and Wang Taiheng also wrote to Shi Miyuan, demanding that Feng Rong and Wang Hu be punished for failing to fight the fire with all their strength, and that Lin Jie, acting prefect of Lin'an, and Zhao Rudan, transport commissioner of the Two Zhes, be penalized as well.

sentences.zh: 人皆壯之。

translations.literal: Everyone admired their boldness.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it admired their courage.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，獨為袁燮議謚，餘皆閣筆，因嘆曰：“幽、厲雖百世不改，謚有美惡，豈諛墓比哉？”

translations.literal: Promoted to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he alone deliberated Yuan Xie's posthumous name while the rest laid down their pens. He sighed and said: "You and Li, though a hundred generations pass, are not altered—but posthumous names have fair and foul kinds; they are hardly comparable to flattery on a tomb, are they?"
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he alone argued Yuan Xie's posthumous name while the others refused to write. He sighed: "Kings You and Li keep their ill names through the ages—posthumous titles can honor or condemn. That is not the same as flattering a tomb inscription, is it?"

sentences.zh: 會朱端常子乞謚，塤曰：“端常居臺諫則逐善類，為藩牧則務刻剝，宜得惡謚，以戒後來。”

translations.literal: When Zhu Duanchang's son requested a posthumous name, Xun said: "As a censor Duanchang drove out good men; as a regional governor he was devoted to exploitation—he deserves an ill name to warn those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Duanchang's son petitioned for a posthumous title, Chen Xun said: "As a censor Duanchang expelled worthy men; as a regional governor he squeezed the people dry. He deserves a bad name to warn posterity."

sentences.zh: 乃謚曰「榮愿」。

translations.literal: They then gave the posthumous name Rongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They posthumously named him Rongyuan—"Glory-desiring"—an ironic condemnation.

sentences.zh: 議出，宰相而下皆肅然改容。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was issued, from the chief counselor down all changed countenance with solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: When the decision was announced, every official from the chief counselor down sat up with sober faces.

sentences.zh: 考功郎陳耆覆議，合宦者陳洵益欲改，塤終不答。

translations.literal: Review Officer Chen Qi reheard the case; together with the eunuch Chen Xunyi they wished to change it, but Xun never replied.
translations.idiomatic: Review Officer Chen Qi reopened the deliberation; he and the eunuch Chen Xunyi wanted the name changed, but Chen Xun would not answer.

sentences.zh: 李全在楚州有異志，塤以書告彌遠：“痛加警悔，以回群心。

translations.literal: Li Quan at Chuzhou harbored disloyal intentions. Xun wrote to Miyuan: "Apply stern warning and repentance to win back the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan at Chuzhou was showing rebellious intent. Chen Xun wrote to Shi Miyuan: "Strike hard with warning and repentance to win back the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 蚤正典刑，以肅權綱。

translations.literal: Promptly apply standard punishments to tighten the bonds of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Punish swiftly under the law to restore discipline among the powerful.

sentences.zh: 大明黜陟，以飭政體。”

translations.literal: Make promotions and dismissals brilliantly clear to rectify the framework of governance."
translations.idiomatic: Make rewards and removals unmistakably clear to set the body politic straight."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: His advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賈貴妃入內，塤又言：“乞去君側之蠱媚，以正主德；

translations.literal: Before long the Honored Consort Jia entered the inner palace. Xun again said: "I beg you to remove bewitching flatterers at the ruler's side to correct the ruler's virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Consort Jia entered the inner palace. Chen Xun spoke again: "Remove the seductive favorites at the sovereign's side and restore the ruler's virtue;

sentences.zh: 從天下之公論，以新庶政。”

translations.literal: follow the public judgment of the realm to renew ordinary governance."
translations.idiomatic: follow the consensus of the realm and renew everyday governance."

sentences.zh: 彌遠召塤問之曰：“吾甥殆好名邪？”

translations.literal: Miyuan summoned Xun and asked: "My nephew—does he perhaps love reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan summoned Chen Xun and asked: "Nephew, are you perhaps chasing a name for yourself?"

sentences.zh: 塤曰：“好名，孟子所不取也。

translations.literal: Xun said: "Loving reputation—Mencius would not approve of that.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun replied: "Chasing reputation is what Mencius rejected.

sentences.zh: 夫求士於三代之上，惟恐其好名；

translations.literal: In seeking gentlemen from the age before the Three Dynasties, one feared only that they loved reputation;
translations.idiomatic: In the age before the Three Dynasties, when seeking worthy men one feared only that they cared too much for fame;

sentences.zh: 求士於三代之下，惟恐其不好名耳。”

translations.literal: in seeking gentlemen from the age after the Three Dynasties, one fears only that they do not love reputation."
translations.idiomatic: in the age since, one fears only that they do not care for fame at all."

sentences.zh: 力丐去，添差通判嘉興府。

translations.literal: He pressed hard to leave and was given an additional assignment as Vice Prefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on leaving office and was given an additional appointment as Vice Prefect of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 彌遠卒，召為樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: When Miyuan died, he was summoned as compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Miyuan died, he was recalled as a compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 入對，首言：“天下之安危在宰相。

translations.literal: At an audience he began by saying: "The safety and peril of the realm lie with the chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: At court he opened by saying: "The realm's safety or ruin rests on whoever sits as chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 南渡以來，屢失機會。

translations.literal: Since the move south, opportunities have repeatedly been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court moved south, chance after chance has been squandered.

sentences.zh: 秦檜死，所任不過萬俟禼、沈該耳。

translations.literal: When Qin Gui died, those appointed were no more than Wan Qixie and Shen Gai.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Gui died, the throne turned only to Wan Qixie and Shen Gai.

sentences.zh: 侂胄死，所任史彌遠耳。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou died, the one appointed was Shi Miyuan alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou fell, the throne turned only to Shi Miyuan.

sentences.zh: 此今日所當謹也。”

translations.literal: This is what must be guarded against today."
translations.idiomatic: That is the pattern the court must guard against now."

sentences.zh: 次言：“內廷當嚴宦官之禁，外廷當嚴臺諫之選。”

translations.literal: Next he said: "The inner court should strictly restrict eunuchs; the outer court should strictly select censors."
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "The inner court must keep eunuchs on a tight rein; the outer court must choose censors with care."

sentences.zh: 於是洵益陰中之，監察御史王定劾塤，出知常州，改衢州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xunyi secretly slandered him; Supervising Censor Wang Ding impeached Xun. He was sent out as prefect of Changzhou, then transferred to Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xunyi then worked against him in secret; Supervising Censor Wang Ding impeached Chen Xun, who was sent out to govern Changzhou and then transferred to Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 寇卜日發漈坑，遵江山縣而東。

translations.literal: The bandits chose a day to set out from Jikeng and proceed east along Jiangshan County.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fixed a day to march from Jikeng and move east through Jiangshan County.

sentences.zh: 塤獲諜者，即遣人致牛酒諭之曰：“汝不為良民而為劫盜，不事耒耜而弄甲兵，今享汝牛酒，冀汝改業，否則殺無赦。”

translations.literal: Xun captured a spy and immediately sent men with cattle and wine to instruct him: "You do not become good subjects but become robbers; you do not take up the plow but wield arms. Today I give you cattle and wine, hoping you will change your trade—otherwise execution without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun seized a spy and at once sent envoys with cattle and wine, telling the bandits: "You refuse honest livelihood and turn to robbery; you leave the plow for weapons. Take this cattle and wine and return to honest work—or die without mercy."

sentences.zh: 於是自首者日以百數，獻器械者重酬之，遂以潰散。

translations.literal: Then those who surrendered themselves numbered in the hundreds daily; those who turned in weapons were richly rewarded, and the bandits thus scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Within days hundreds were surrendering each day; those who handed over weapons were paid well, and the bandit force broke apart.

sentences.zh: 改提點都大坑冶，徙福建轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner for the Chief Mining Offices and moved to Transport Judge of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Commissioner for the Chief Mining Offices, he was then made Transport Judge of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 侍御史蔣峴常與論《中庸》，不合，又劾之。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Jiang Xian often debated the Doctrine of the Mean with him; they did not agree, and Jiang impeached him again.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Jiang Xian often argued the Doctrine of the Mean with him; when they clashed, Jiang impeached him once more.

sentences.zh: 主管崇道觀。

translations.literal: He was assigned to administer the Chongdao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of the Chongdao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遷浙西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，盜起，捕斬之，盜懼徙去。

translations.literal: In a year of drought bandits rose; he captured and executed them, and the bandits, in fear, moved away.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year bandits appeared; he captured and executed them, and the rest fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 安吉州俞垓與丞相李宗勉連姻，恃勢黷貨，塤親按臨之。

translations.literal: Yu Gai of Anji Prefecture was connected by marriage to Chief Counselor Li Zongmian and, relying on his power, traded in illicit goods. Xun personally went to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gai of Anji was related by marriage to Chief Counselor Li Zongmian and, backed by that connection, profited from corruption. Chen Xun went in person to investigate.

sentences.zh: 弓手戴福以獲潘丙功為副尉，宗勉倚之為腹心，盜橫貪害，塤至，福聞風而去。

translations.literal: The archer Dai Fu, for capturing the bandit Pan Bing, had been made deputy district captain. Zongmian relied on him as a trusted confidant; he plundered and harmed with impunity. When Xun arrived, Fu fled at the first rumor.
translations.idiomatic: The bowman Dai Fu had been made deputy district captain for capturing the bandit Pan Bing. Li Zongmian treated him as a trusted henchman, and Fu robbed and abused people at will. When Chen Xun arrived, Fu fled at the first word.

sentences.zh: 貽書宗勉曰：“塤治福，所以報丞相也。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Zongmian saying: "In punishing Fu, Xun is repaying the chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Li Zongmian: "By prosecuting Fu I am doing the chief counselor a service.

sentences.zh: 傳間實走丞相，賢輔弼不宜有此。”

translations.literal: Rumor in fact says he fled to the chief counselor—a worthy assistant should not have such a man."
translations.idiomatic: Word has it he ran straight to your house—a worthy minister should not shelter such a man."

sentences.zh: 宗勉答書曰：“福罪惡貫盈，非君不能治。

translations.literal: Zongmian replied: "Fu's crimes fill the measure; without you he could not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmian answered: "Fu's crimes are overflowing; without you he could not be brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 宗勉雖不才，不敢庇奸兇。

translations.literal: Though Zongmian is without talent, he dares not shield villains.
translations.idiomatic: I may lack talent, but I will not shield a villain.

sentences.zh: 惟君留意。”

translations.literal: Only ask that you give the matter your attention."
translations.idiomatic: I leave the matter in your hands."

sentences.zh: 及獲福豫章，眾皆欲殺之，塤曰：“若是則刑濫矣。”

translations.literal: When Fu was captured at Yuzhang, everyone wanted to kill him. Xun said: "If we did that, punishment would be excessive."
translations.idiomatic: When Dai Fu was taken at Yuzhang, everyone wanted him executed. Chen Xun said: "That would make the penalty too broad."

sentences.zh: 乃加墨徇於市，囚之圜土。

translations.literal: He then had him tattooed and paraded through the market and imprisoned in the round earthwork.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he had Fu tattooed and displayed in the marketplace, then confined in the round prison.

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎召，及為國子司業，諸生鹹相慶，以為得師。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, when he became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education the students all rejoiced together, thinking they had gained a true teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and then appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, the students celebrated, believing they had found a worthy teacher.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼玉牒檢討、國史編修、實錄修撰，乃辭兼史館。

translations.literal: Before long he concurrently served as collator of the imperial genealogy, compiler of the national history, and compiler of the veritable records, then declined the concurrent post at the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held concurrent posts collating the imperial genealogy, compiling the national history, and compiling the veritable records, but declined the History Office assignment.

sentences.zh: 歷陳境土之蹙，民生之艱，國計之匱，“既無經理圖回之素，惟有感動轉移之策，必有為之本者，本者何？

translations.literal: He enumerated in detail the shrinking of the territory, the hardship of the people, and the emptiness of state finances: "Having no long-standing plan for ordering affairs, there remains only the policy of moving hearts through moral influence. There must be a root for action—what is the root?
translations.idiomatic: He laid out at length how the borders had shrunk, the people suffered, and the treasury ran dry: "With no steady plan for governing, only the strategy of moving hearts by moral example remains. Action must have a root—what is that root?

sentences.zh: 復此心之妙耳”。

translations.literal: To restore the subtlety of this heart alone."
translations.idiomatic: To recover the subtlety of the heart itself."

sentences.zh: 又言：“履泰安而逸樂者，有習安致危之理。

translations.literal: He also said: "Those who tread peace and ease in comfort contain within themselves the principle by which ease leads to peril.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Those who live in peace and drift into comfort carry within them the logic by which comfort breeds danger.

sentences.zh: 因艱危而兢懼者，有慮危圖安之機。

translations.literal: Those who, because of hardship and peril, become vigilant and fearful contain within themselves the opportunity to plan for security amid danger.
translations.idiomatic: Those who, facing hardship, grow vigilant carry within them the chance to secure safety from danger.

sentences.zh: 明用舍以振紀綱，躬節儉以汰冗濫，屏奸妄以厲將士，抑貴近以寬糶采，結鄉社以防竊發，黜增創以培根本。

translations.literal: Make clear who is employed and who dismissed to revive statutes; practice thrift in person to cut redundant waste; remove wicked impostors to steel officers and soldiers; restrain the high and near to broaden grain purchases and procurement; organize village communities to guard against sudden uprisings; abolish new surcharges to strengthen the root.
translations.idiomatic: Make appointments and dismissals transparent to restore discipline; practice austerity to cut waste; drive out deceivers to stiffen troops; curb the privileged to ease grain levies; organize village communities against sudden unrest; abolish new taxes to strengthen the foundation.

sentences.zh: 今任用混殽，薰蕕同器，遂使賢者恥與同群。”

translations.literal: Today appointments are confused, fragrant and foul in the same vessel, so that worthy men are ashamed to stand among them."
translations.idiomatic: Today appointments are muddled—worthies and scoundrels packed together—until good men are ashamed to belong to the same company."

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫金淵見之，怒。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Officer Jin Yuan saw it and grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Officer Jin Yuan read it and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 塤乞補外，不許，又辭免和糴轉官賞，亦不許。

translations.literal: Xun begged for an outside appointment and was not permitted; he also declined promotion rewards for the grain-purchase service and was again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun asked to serve outside the capital and was refused; he also tried to decline promotion rewards tied to the grain-purchase program and was refused again.

sentences.zh: 知溫州，未上，以言罷。

translations.literal: Appointed prefect of Wenzhou, before he took up the post he was dismissed because of his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Named prefect of Wenzhou, he was removed from office for his words before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 塤家居，時自娛於泉石，四方學者踵至。

translations.literal: Living at home, Xun at times amused himself among springs and rocks; scholars from all quarters came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At home Chen Xun took quiet pleasure in landscape and stone; students arrived from every direction.

sentences.zh: 輕財急義，明白洞達，一言之出，終身可復。

translations.literal: He was generous with wealth and urgent in righteousness, clear and penetrating in judgment; a word once spoken could be trusted for a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: He gave freely and acted swiftly for justice, saw matters with lucid clarity, and spoke words one could trust for a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 忽臥疾，戒其子抽架上書占之，得《呂祖謙文集》，其《墓志》曰：“祖謙生於丁巳歲，沒於辛丑歲。”

translations.literal: Suddenly he fell ill and instructed his son to take a book from the shelf and divine by it; he obtained Lü Zuqian's collected works, whose "Epitaph" reads: "Zuqian was born in the dingsi year and died in the xinchou year."
translations.idiomatic: He suddenly fell ill and told his son to pull a book from the shelf and read an omen from it; the volume was Lü Zuqian's collected works, whose epitaph says: "Zuqian was born in the year dingsi and died in the year xinchou."

sentences.zh: 塤曰：“異哉！

translations.literal: Xun said: "How strange!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun said: "How strange!

sentences.zh: 我生於慶元丁巳，今歲在辛丑，於是一甲矣。

translations.literal: I was born in dingsi of the Qingyuan era; this year is xinchou—a full sexagenary cycle has passed.
translations.idiomatic: I was born in dingsi of the Qingyuan reign; this year is xinchou—the same cycle has come round.

sentences.zh: 吾死矣夫！”

translations.literal: I am about to die!"
translations.idiomatic: My time has come!"

sentences.zh: 子蒙，年十八，上書萬言論國事。

translations.literal: Zimeng, at eighteen, submitted a memorial of ten thousand characters discussing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zimeng, at eighteen, submitted a ten-thousand-character memorial on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 吳子良奇之，妻以女。

translations.literal: Wu Ziliang marveled at him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ziliang was impressed and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 為太府寺主簿。

translations.literal: He served as chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 入對，極言賈似道為相時國政闕失，文多不錄。

translations.literal: At an audience he spoke at length on the failures of state administration when Jia Sidao was chief counselor; most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: At court he spoke at length about the failures of government under Jia Sidao as chief counselor; most of what he said was omitted from the record.

sentences.zh: 為淮東總領，似道誣以貪汙，貶建昌軍簿，錄其家，惟青氈耳。

translations.literal: Serving as overall commander of Huaidong, Sidao falsely charged him with corruption, had him demoted to clerk of Jianchang Army, and searched his household—finding only a plain wool mat.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as overall fiscal commander of Huaidong, he was falsely accused of corruption by Jia Sidao, demoted to clerk of Jianchang Army, and had his home searched—all they found was a single plain wool mat.

sentences.zh: 德祐初，禮部侍郎李玨乞放便，以刑部侍郎召，不赴，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Deyou, Vice Minister of Rites Li Jue requested that he be released to private life; he was summoned as Vice Minister of Punishments but did not go, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Deyou era, Vice Minister of Rites Li Jue asked that he be allowed to retire; the court summoned him as Vice Minister of Punishments, but he did not go, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 趙與芮，字德淵，太祖十世孫。

translations.literal: Zhao Yurui, courtesy name Deyuan, was a tenth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yurui, whose courtesy name was Deyuan, was a tenth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 居湖州。

translations.literal: He resided in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1220.

sentences.zh: 歷官差主管官告院，遷將作監主簿，差知嘉興府，遷知大宗正兼權樞密院檢詳諸房文字，尋為都官郎官，加直寶章閣、兩浙轉運判官。

translations.literal: He successively served by assignment as administrator of the Office of Patent Letters, was promoted to chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works, assigned as prefect of Jiaxing, promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent authority as reviewer of documents in all bureaus of the Bureau of Military Affairs, soon became an official of the Ministry of Justice, and was given the additional titles of Directly Attached to the Hall of Precious Documents and Transport Judge of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through a series of posts: administrator of the Office of Patent Letters, chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works, prefect of Jiaxing, Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent review duties at the Bureau of Military Affairs, then an official of the Ministry of Justice, with added titles as Directly Attached to the Hall of Precious Documents and Transport Judge of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 進煥章閣、知慶元府，主管沿海制置司公事，拜司農少卿，仍兼知慶元府兼沿海制置副使。

translations.literal: Promoted to the Hall of Illustrious Documents and appointed prefect of Qingyuan, he administered the affairs of the Coastal Pacification Commission, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, and still concurrently served as prefect of Qingyuan and Deputy Commissioner of Coastal Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to the Hall of Illustrious Documents and made prefect of Qingyuan, he directed the Coastal Pacification Commission, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, and continued to govern Qingyuan as deputy coastal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷浙西提點刑獄，授中書門下省檢正諸房公事，拜司農卿兼知臨安府，主管浙西安撫司公事，權刑部侍郎兼詳定敕令官，權兵部侍郎，遷戶部侍郎，權戶部尚書，時暫兼吏部尚書，尋為真，兼戶部尚書，時暫兼浙西提舉常平，加端明殿學士、提領戶部財用，皆依舊兼知臨安府。

translations.literal: Promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Western Zhe, appointed collator in the Secretariat-Chancellery, appointed Minister of Revenue with concurrent appointment as prefect of Lin'an, administrator of the Western Zhe Pacification Commission, Acting Vice Minister of Punishments with concurrent service as Commissioner for the Revision of Statutes, Acting Vice Minister of War, promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, Acting Minister of Revenue, for a time also Acting Minister of Personnel, soon made permanent with concurrent appointment as Minister of Revenue, for a time also concurrently Intendant of the Western Zhe Ever-Normal Granaries, given the additional titles of Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and Commissioner for Revenue Affairs of the Ministry of Revenue—all while still concurrently serving as prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Western Zhe, then collator in the Secretariat-Chancellery, Minister of Revenue while also governing Lin'an and directing the Western Zhe Pacification Commission, Acting Vice Minister of Punishments with concurrent duties revising statutes, Acting Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Revenue, Acting Minister of Revenue, briefly Acting Minister of Personnel, then confirmed in office while retaining the Ministry of Revenue, briefly Intendant of Western Zhe Ever-Normal Granaries, and finally Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and Commissioner for Revenue Affairs—through all of this still serving as prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 與執政恩澤，加資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: Along with the chief administrator's favor he was given the additional title of Grand Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Sharing in the chief administrator's favor, he received the added title Grand Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿學士知紹興府、浙東安撫使；

translations.literal: As Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture he served as prefect of Shaoxing and Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhe;
translations.idiomatic: As Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture he governed Shaoxing as Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhe;

sentences.zh: 知平江府兼淮、浙發運使，時暫兼權浙西提點刑獄；

translations.literal: as prefect of Pingjiang with concurrent appointment as Transport Commissioner for Huai and the Two Zhes, for a time also concurrently Acting Judicial Commissioner of Western Zhe;
translations.idiomatic: as prefect of Pingjiang and Transport Commissioner for Huai and the Two Zhes, briefly also Acting Judicial Commissioner of Western Zhe;

sentences.zh: 授沿江制置使，知建康府、江東安撫使、馬步軍都總管兼行宮留守，節制和州、無為軍、安慶府三郡屯田使；

translations.literal: appointed Pacification Commissioner along the Yangzi, prefect of Jiankang, Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong, overall commander of infantry and cavalry, concurrently Palatial Intendant, and controller of the garrison commissioners of Hezhou, Wuwei Army, and Anqing Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: appointed Yangzi Pacification Commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong, overall commander of infantry and cavalry, Palatial Intendant, and controller of garrison affairs at Hezhou, Wuwei Army, and Anqing;

sentences.zh: 時暫兼權揚州、兩淮安撫制置使，改兼知揚州，尋兼知鎮江府，兼淮東總領，提舉洞霄宮；

translations.literal: for a time also concurrently Acting Pacification Commissioner of Yangzhou and the Two Huai, changed to concurrent prefect of Yangzhou, soon also concurrently prefect of Zhenjiang, concurrently Overall Fiscal Commander of Huaidong, and Administrator of the Dongxiao Palace;
translations.idiomatic: briefly also Acting Pacification Commissioner of Yangzhou and the Two Huai, then concurrently prefect of Yangzhou, soon also prefect of Zhenjiang, Overall Fiscal Commander of Huaidong, and Administrator of the Dongxiao Palace;

sentences.zh: 復為淮、浙發運使，差知平江府，特轉兩官致仕。

translations.literal: Again appointed Transport Commissioner for Huai and the Two Zhes, assigned as prefect of Pingjiang, and specially promoted two ranks to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Transport Commissioner for Huai and the Two Zhes, was assigned prefect of Pingjiang, and received a special promotion of two ranks before retiring.

sentences.zh: 景定元年八月，卒，特贈少師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Jingding he died, and was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In August 1260 he died and was posthumously granted the title of Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 與芮所至急於財利，幾於聚斂之臣矣。

translations.literal: Wherever Yurui went he was eager for wealth and profit, nearly a minister who amassed revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Zhao Yurui served he was obsessed with profit, making him almost a classic revenue-extraction official.

sentences.zh: 李大同，字從仲，婺州東陽人。

translations.literal: Li Datong, courtesy name Congzhong, was a man of Dongyang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Datong, whose courtesy name was Congzhong, was a native of Dongyang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1223.

sentences.zh: 歷官為秘書丞兼崇政殿說書，拜右正言兼侍講。

translations.literal: He successively served as Assistant Director of the Palace Library with concurrent appointment as Lecturer at the Hall for the Veneration of Governance, and was appointed Right Remonstrator with concurrent service as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts including Assistant Director of the Palace Library and Lecturer at the Hall for the Veneration of Governance, and was appointed Right Remonstrator while also serving as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 疏言：“趙、冀分野，乃有熒惑犯填星之變，則我師之出，豈無當長慮而卻顧者。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "In the astral territories of Zhao and Ji there has occurred the omen of the Sparkling Deluder transgressing Saturn; when our armies march out, should we not have those who take long thought and look back?
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "In the Zhao and Ji celestial divisions Mars has transgressed Saturn—a portent that should give us pause before sending our armies abroad.

sentences.zh: 故臣願陛下勿以星文為小異而或加忽。

translations.literal: Thus your subject wishes Your Majesty not to treat these celestial writings as minor anomalies and perhaps slight them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I urge Your Majesty not to dismiss such celestial signs as minor irregularities.

sentences.zh: 一話一語，一政一事，必求有以格天心而弭災變。

translations.literal: Every word and phrase, every policy and affair, must seek means to accord with Heaven's heart and quell calamitous changes.
translations.idiomatic: In every word spoken and every measure taken, we must seek to align with Heaven's will and avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 至於進兵攻討，尤切謹重。”

translations.literal: As for advancing troops in attack and suppression, this is especially to be done with utmost caution and seriousness."
translations.idiomatic: Military campaigns in particular demand the greatest caution and restraint."

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿兼國史編修、實錄檢討，兼侍講，兼權侍立修註官，遷起居郎，拜殿中侍御史，權刑部侍郎兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，選吏部侍郎，進工部尚書，以寶謨閣直學士知平江府，提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent service as Compiler of the National History and Collator of the Veritable Records, Lecturer-in-Waiting, concurrently Acting Attending Scribe for the Daily Record, promoted to Gentleman for Proper Service, appointed Censor-in-Chief within the Palace, Acting Vice Minister of Punishments with concurrent service as Co-Compiler of the National History and Co-Compiler for the Veritable Records Academy, selected Vice Minister of Personnel, advanced to Minister of Works, as Directly Attached to the Hall of Treasured Counsel made prefect of Pingjiang, and Administrator of the Taiping Xingguo Palace at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while compiling the National History and collating the Veritable Records, served as Lecturer-in-Waiting and Acting Attending Scribe for the Daily Record, became Gentleman for Proper Service and Censor-in-Chief within the Palace, Acting Vice Minister of Punishments with concurrent historiographical duties, Vice Minister of Personnel, Minister of Works, Directly Attached to the Hall of Treasured Counsel as prefect of Pingjiang, and Administrator of the Taiping Xingguo Palace at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕，不許，後卒於家。

translations.literal: He requested retirement, was not permitted, and later died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire but was refused, and later died at home.

sentences.zh: 黃┿，字子耕，隆興分寧人。

translations.literal: Huang Xun, courtesy name Zigeng, was a man of Fenning in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xun, whose courtesy name was Zigeng, was a native of Fenning in Longxing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗從郭雍、朱熹學，熹深期之，而┿亦以道自任，反復論辯，必無所疑然後止。

translations.literal: He once studied under Guo Yong and Zhu Xi; Xi greatly expected much of him, and Xun also took the Way as his charge, arguing back and forth until no doubt remained and only then stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Guo Yong and Zhu Xi, who held him in high expectation; Xun likewise devoted himself to the Way, debating points back and forth until every doubt was resolved.

sentences.zh: 舉太學進士，為瑞昌主簿，監文思院，知盧陽縣，五溪獠獷悍，┿為詩諭之，獠感悅，有公事莫敢違。

translations.literal: Raised as a Metropolitan Examination jinshi, he served as chief clerk of Ruichang, Superintendent of the Bureau of Literary and Artistic Works, and magistrate of Luyang County; the Liao of the Five Streams were wild and fierce—Xun composed poems to instruct them, and the Liao were moved and pleased, so that in public affairs none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the Metropolitan Examination he served as chief clerk of Ruichang, Superintendent of the Bureau of Literary and Artistic Works, and magistrate of Luyang; the fierce Liao tribes of the Five Streams he persuaded with poetry, and they responded with such respect that none dared defy official orders.

sentences.zh: 通判處州，經、總制有額無錢，俗號殿最綱，┿會十年中成賦酌取之，閣免逋負，錢額鈞等，獨以最聞。

translations.literal: As Assistant Prefect of Chuzhou, the economic and overall fiscal categories had quotas but no funds, popularly called the "Hall and Bottom quota"; Xun calculated them from ten years of completed tax assessments and took amounts accordingly, suspended arrears, equalized the money quotas, and alone became famed as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: As Assistant Prefect of Chuzhou he tackled the notorious "top-and-bottom quota" system, under which fiscal targets existed on paper but without funding; drawing on a decade of completed tax assessments, he set proportional levies, suspended arrears, and equalized quotas—earning the highest reputation of any official in the region.

sentences.zh: 主管官告院、大理寺簿、軍器監丞，歲餘三遷，┿乃不樂。

translations.literal: Administrator of the Office of Patent Letters, clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, and assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments—within little more than a year three promotions, yet Xun was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrator of the Office of Patent Letters, clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, and assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments; though promoted three times in just over a year, Xun found no satisfaction in such advancement.

sentences.zh: 間行西湖，慨然曰：“我昔在南、北山，一水一石，無不自題品，今無復情味，何邪？”

translations.literal: Walking beside West Lake he sighed and said: "In former days on the southern and northern hills, every stream and rock I myself inscribed and appraised—why is there no savor in it now?"
translations.idiomatic: Strolling by West Lake he sighed: "Once, among the southern and northern hills, I inscribed and commented on every stream and stone; why do they hold no charm for me now?"

sentences.zh: 丐外，知臺州。

translations.literal: He requested an outside appointment and was made prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a provincial post, he was appointed prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 謝良佐子孫居臺者既播越流落，┿求之民間，收而教之。

translations.literal: The descendants of Xie Liangzuo who lived in Taizhou had been scattered and cast adrift; Xun sought them among the people, gathered them in, and taught them.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of Xie Liangzuo who had lived in Taizhou had been scattered in hardship; Xun searched them out among the common people, took them in, and instructed them.

sentences.zh: 勤苦夙夜，先勸後禁，訟牒銷縮，郡稱平治。

translations.literal: Diligent from early to late, he first persuaded and afterward forbade; legal petitions dwindled, and the prefecture was called peaceful and well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Working tirelessly day and night, he led through persuasion before resorting to prohibition; lawsuits declined sharply and the prefecture came to be known as orderly and at peace.

sentences.zh: 為濟糶倉，為抵當庫，葬民之棲寄暴露者為棺千五百，置養濟院，又創安濟坊以居病囚，皆自有子本錢，使不廢。

translations.literal: He established relief granaries and pawn offices, buried fifteen hundred common folk whose remains had been exposed in lodgings, set up a hospice, and also founded an infirmary to house sick prisoners—all with their own capital funds so they would not fail.
translations.idiomatic: He established relief granaries and pawn offices, provided coffins for fifteen hundred exposed corpses of the destitute, founded a hospice, and created an infirmary for sick prisoners—each institution endowed with its own operating capital so they would remain in perpetual service.

sentences.zh: 故葉適謂┿條目建置，憂民如家。

translations.literal: Therefore Ye Shi said that Xun's detailed institutions and establishments showed concern for the people like a family.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Shi remarked that Xun's systematic programs of public welfare showed a concern for the people as if for his own household.

sentences.zh: 遷袁州，哭從弟哀甚，得疾卒。

translations.literal: Transferred to Yuanzhou, he wept bitterly for a younger cousin, took ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yuanzhou, he grieved so deeply over a younger male cousin that he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 所著有《復齋集》。

translations.literal: His writings include the Collection of the Fuzhai Studio.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works survive as the Fuzhai Collection.

sentences.zh: 楊大異，字同伯，唐天平節度使漢公之後，十世祖祥避地醴陵，因家焉。

translations.literal: Yang Dayi, courtesy name Tongbo, was a descendant of Han Gong, military commissioner of Tianping under Tang; his tenth-generation ancestor Xiang fled to Liling and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dayi, whose courtesy name was Tongbo, descended from Han Gong, Tang dynasty military commissioner of Tianping; his tenth-generation ancestor Xiang sought refuge at Liling and settled there.

sentences.zh: 祥事親孝，親亡哀毀，泣盡繼以血，廬墓終身，有白芝、白烏、白兔之瑞。

translations.literal: Xiang was filial toward his parents; when they died he mourned to emaciation, wept until tears gave way to blood, lived in a mourning hut by the tomb for life, and there were auspicious signs of white fungus, white crows, and white rabbits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was deeply filial; after his parents' deaths he mourned until wasted away, weeping until tears were replaced by blood, and maintained a mourning hut by their tomb for life—during which white fungus, white crows, and white rabbits appeared as auspicious omens.

sentences.zh: 事聞於朝，褒封至孝公，賜名木植墓道，以旌其孝。

translations.literal: The matter reached the court; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Utmost Filiality, given precious trees planted along the tomb road, to commend his filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court he was enfeoffed as Duke of Utmost Filiality, and precious trees were planted along the tomb path to honor his devotion.

sentences.zh: 大異從胡宏受《春秋》大義。

translations.literal: Dayi received the grand principles of the Spring and Autumn from Hu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi studied the essential teachings of the Spring and Autumn Annals under Hu Hong.

sentences.zh: 登嘉定十三年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1220.

sentences.zh: 授衡陽主簿，有惠政。

translations.literal: Appointed chief clerk of Hengyang, he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed chief clerk of Hengyang, he governed with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 調龍泉尉，攝邑令。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Longquan, he acted as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the post of Longquan county captain, he also served as acting county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 適歲饑，提刑司遣吏和糴米二萬石於邑，米價頓增，民乏食，大異即以提刑司所糴者如價發糶，民甚德之。

translations.literal: Just then there was famine; the Judicial Commission dispatched clerks to purchase by agreement twenty thousand shi of rice in the county, rice prices suddenly rose, and the people lacked food; Dayi immediately released for sale at market price the rice the Judicial Commission had purchased, and the people greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year the Judicial Commission sent clerks to procure twenty thousand shi of rice in the county, driving prices sharply upward and leaving the people short of food; Dayi immediately sold the Commission's stock at market price, earning the people's deep gratitude.

sentences.zh: 提刑趙與芮大怒，捃其罪弗得，坐以方命，移安遠尉。

translations.literal: Judicial Commissioner Zhao Yurui was greatly enraged; unable to gather charges against him, he punished him for defiance of orders and transferred him to captain of Anyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial Commissioner Zhao Yurui was furious; finding no actionable charges against him, he punished Dayi for insubordination and reassigned him as captain of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 邑有峒寇擾民，官兵致討，積年弗獲，檄大異往治之。

translations.literal: In the county cave bandits harassed the people; government troops pursued them, and for years could not capture them; an order was sent for Dayi to go govern the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cave bandits had harassed the county for years despite repeated military campaigns; finally an order went out for Dayi to handle the situation.

sentences.zh: 大異以一仆負告身自隨，肩輿入賊峒，傳呼尉至，賊露刃成列以待，徐諭以禍福，皆伏地叩頭，願改過自新。

translations.literal: Dayi took one servant carrying his patent of appointment, entered the bandits' cave in a sedan chair, announced that the captain had arrived; the bandits bared blades and formed ranks to await him; he slowly instructed them on fortune and misfortune, and all prostrated themselves kowtowing, wishing to reform and start anew.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi took only one servant carrying his commission of office and entered the bandits' lair in a sedan chair; when heralds announced the captain's arrival the bandits drew blades and lined up to receive him, but he calmly lectured them on the consequences of their conduct until all prostrated themselves and vowed to reform.

sentences.zh: 留告身為質，偕其渠魁數輩出降。
